parts.ms: B1 60 m/s at t = 15; B1ft 60 + T; M1 equate distances (areas) with correct structure, e.g. ½×15×60 + ½T(60 + 60 + T) = 40(15 + T); A2 correct, −1 each error; A1 k = 40. Taking T as the end time instead of 15 + T: max B1B1ft M1A0A0A0 (MS p.12)

parts.ms: M1 Pythagoras; A1 √101 — A0 if only a decimal (MS p.13)

parts.ask: Find, in degrees, the angle between F and the vector i + j
parts.ms: M1 trig ratio for α (tan α = 1/10); B1 45° seen; M1 difference 45° − α; A1 39.289… (scalar product or cosine rule alternatives) (MS p.13)

parts.ask: Resultant of F and (−15i + aj) N is parallel to but opposite to 2i − 3j: find a
parts.ms: B1 resultant −5i + (a + 1)j; M1 ratio equation from the resultant (M0 if equated to 2i − 3j or ratio upside down); A1 (a + 1)/(−5) = −3/2; M1 solve; A1 6.5 (MS p.13)

parts.ask: A (4 kg) on a rough table, string over a smooth light pulley at the edge to B (3 kg), 1.4 m above the floor; B hits the floor after 2 s: show the acceleration is 0.7 m/s²
parts.ms: M1 1.4 = ½a × 2²; A1* given answer (MS p.14)

parts.ask: State which modelling assumption you used in (a)
parts.ms: B1 inextensibility of the string; B0 with extras (MS p.14)

parts.ask: Find the magnitude of the resultant force exerted on the pulley by the string
parts.ms: M1A1 for B: 3g − T = 3 × 0.7 (T = 27.3); M1 resultant 2T cos 45° or √(T² + T²); A1 39 or 38.6 (MS p.14)

parts.ask: Coefficient of friction between A and the table is μ: find μ
parts.ms: M1A1 for A: T − F = 4 × 0.7 (or system 3g − F = 7 × 0.7); B1 R = 4g; B1 F = μR; DM1 solve for μ (DM0 if T = 3g used); A1 0.625 or 0.63 — the exact 5/8 is A0 (MS pp.14–15)

parts.ask: Determine, by calculation, whether or not A reaches the pulley
parts.final_form: A stops 0.16 m after B lands; 1.4 + 0.16 < 2 so it does not reach the pulley
parts.ms: M1 speed when B lands (1.4 m/s); M1 new equation of motion for A, −μ·4g = 4a; M1 complete method for distance to stop (needs new deceleration); A1 0.16 or 0.159; A1cso conclusion with "< 2" seen. Alternative: v² at the pulley negative (MS pp.14–15)

parts.ask: P (m, speed 4u) catches Q (2m, speed u) moving the same way; afterwards both move the same way and Q's speed is four times P's: find Q's speed after the collision
parts.ms: M1 CLM 4mu + 2mu = mv + 2m(4v), condone sign errors; A1 correct; A1 8u/3, positive single term (MS p.6)

parts.ask: Find the magnitude of the impulse exerted by Q on P
parts.ms: M1 impulse-momentum for P (m, 4u, their v_P) or Q (2m, u, their v_Q), difference of momenta, M0 with g; A1ft correct expression (A0 if equal speeds assumed); A1 10mu/3, positive (MS p.6)

parts.ask: State clearly the direction of this impulse
parts.final_form: opposite to the direction of motion
parts.ms: B1 any clear equivalent (MS p.6)

parts.ask: Ball thrown vertically up at 14.7 m/s from 19.6 m above the ground: find the total time until it first hits the ground
parts.ms: M1 complete method, e.g. −19.6 = 14.7t − 4.9t² (or in stages: t₁ = 1.5, s₁ = 11.025, 30.625 = 4.9t₂²); A1 M(A)1 equations, −1 each error; A1 4 only — combining the two quadratic roots is A0 (MS pp.7–8)

parts.ask: Find the speed immediately before it hits the ground
Find the total distance travelled until it first hits the ground
parts.ms: M1 a relevant distance (height gained 11.025 or fall 30.625); A1 correct; M1 total distance 2 × 11.025 + 19.6 (or 2 × 30.625 − 19.6); A1 41.7 or 42 (MS pp.7–8)

parts.ask: Sketch the velocity-time graph until it first hits the ground, stating the coordinates of the start and end points
parts.ms: B1 straight line from the v-axis crossing the t-axis (may be reflected; B0 for a solid vertical line at t = 4); B1 start (0, 14.7); B1ft end (4, −24.5) on their (a), (b) (MS pp.7–8)

parts.ask: Particle 10 kg on a rough plane (tan α = 3/4, μ = 1/2) held in equilibrium by a force P up the slope: find the normal reaction
parts.ms: M1 R = 10g cos α (sin/cos confusion allowed); A1 78.4 or 78 or 8g (MS p.9)

parts.ask: Find the greatest possible value of P
parts.ms: B1 F = 0.5R; M1 P = 10g sin α + F with 10g resolved; A1 correct equation; A1 98 or 10g; an inequality that never becomes an equation max M1A1A0 (MS p.9)

parts.ask: Find the least possible value of P
parts.ms: M1 P = 10g sin α − F; A1 19.6 or 20 or 2g; inequality only max M1A0 (MS p.9)

parts.ask: Non-uniform beam AB, 8 m, mass M, centre of mass d m from A, hung horizontally by vertical ropes at C (AC = 2.5 m) and D (DB = 2 m); gymnast 64 kg at X (AX = 1.875 m) puts it about to tilt about C; gymnast 48 kg at Y (YB = 0.5 m) puts it about to tilt about D: find M
parts.ms: M1 tension at D = 0; M1A1 equation in M and d, e.g. M(C): 64g × 0.625 = Mg(d − 2.5); M1 tension at C = 0; M1A1 M(D): 48g × 1.5 = Mg(6 − d); DM1 solve; A1 32 exact. Other moment points need the remaining tension eliminated (MS pp.10–11)

parts.ask: v = (7 − 5t)i + (12t − 20)j m/s with constant acceleration: find the speed when t = 2
parts.ms: M1 t = 2 gives −3i + 4j; M1 magnitude; A1 5 (MS pp.12–13)

parts.ask: Find, to the nearest degree, the angle between the direction of motion and j when t = 2
parts.ms: M1 relevant trig equation (tan θ = 3/4); A1ft correct on their v; A1 37° or 323° in degrees (MS pp.12–13)

parts.ask: Find the constant acceleration a in terms of i and j
parts.ms: M1 collect t and constant terms (v = (7i − 20j) + t(−5i + 12j)); M1 rearrange to (v − u)/t; A1 −5i + 12j (alternatives: (v − u)/t with two specific velocities, or differentiate M2A1) (MS pp.12–13)

parts.ask: Find t when P moves in the direction of −5i + 8j
parts.ms: M1 ratio of components (reciprocal and a sign error allowed): (7 − 5t)/(12t − 20) = −5/8; A1 correct; M1 solve; A1 2.2 (MS pp.12–13)

parts.ask: Engine 1500 kg pushes truck 500 kg up a slope (sin α = 7/25) via a light rigid coupling with thrust 2000 N; resistances 1200 N and 500 N: find the acceleration
parts.ms: M1 equation of motion in a only with weight resolved, e.g. truck: 2000 − 500 − 500g sin α = 500a; A1 at most one error; A1 correct; A1 0.256 or 0.26, the fraction 32/125 is A0 (MS p.14)

parts.ask: Find the driving force D
parts.ms: M1 system or engine equation in D and a, weight resolved (D − 1200 − 500 − 2000g sin α = 2000a, or D − 1200 − 1500g sin α − 2000 = 1500a); A1 at most one error (omitting g counts as one); A1 correct; A1 7700 (MS p.14)

parts.ms: M1A1 for A: 5mg − T = 5ma; M1A1 for B: T − 3mg = 3ma (M0 if masses missing); DM1 solve for T; A1 T = 15mg/4; M1 force = 2T; A1 15mg/2 (MS p.15)

parts.ask: State how you used the fact that the pulley is smooth
parts.final_form: tension the same on both sides of the pulley
parts.ms: B1 tension is the same on both sides of the pulley; B0 if the pulley is not mentioned or with incorrect extras (MS p.15)

parts.ms: M1 area of the triangle from a v-t graph (½ × 4 × 12); A1 24 (MS p.16)

parts.ask: Find the total distance travelled in the first 26 s
parts.ms: B1 speeds 12 and 42 m/s; M1A1ft trapezium for the next 20 s (540); M1A1ft trapezium for the last 2 s (76); A1 640 cao (MS p.16)

parts.ms: M1 v² = 20² − 2g(−3), must use ±3; A1 21 or 21.4, using 9.8 (MS p.7)

parts.ask: Find the total time from projection until it first strikes the ground
parts.ms: M1 complete method, e.g. −5 = 20t − ½gt² (or up-then-down in stages); A1 M(A)1 for the equation(s), −1 each error; A1 4.3 or 4.32 using 9.8; no isw — adding the roots of a correct quadratic loses the M (MS p.7)

parts.ms: M1 impulse-momentum for P using 2m, difference of momenta, M0 if g included: −5mu = 2m(v − 3u); A1 correct; A1 ½u, positive (MS p.8)

parts.ask: Find the speed of Q after the collision
parts.ms: M1A1 impulse-momentum for Q: 5mu = m(w − (−2u)), or CLM 2m×3u − m×2u = 2m×½u + mw; A1 3u, positive (MS p.8)

parts.ask: Parcel 20 kg on a rough floor (μ = 0.3); forces 200 N at 15° and T N at 25° to the horizontal act in a vertical plane (as in Figure 1): find the smallest T for which it stays in equilibrium
parts.ms: M1A2 vertical: R + 200 sin 15° + T sin 25° = 20g (−1 each error); M1A2 horizontal: 200 cos 15° − T cos 25° − F = 0; B1 F = 0.3R; DM1 solve for T (192.31…); A1 190 or 192; forces and angles must be paired correctly for the M marks (MS p.9)

parts.ask: Non-uniform girder AB, weight W, 6 m, on supports C, D (AC = DB = 1 m); 900 N up at A makes it about to tilt about D; 1500 N up at B makes it about to tilt about C; centre of mass x m from A: find x
parts.ms: M1A1 first tilting equation in W and x with R_C = 0, e.g. M(D): 900 × 5 = W(5 − x); M1A1 second with R_D = 0, e.g. M(C): 1500 × 5 = W(x − 1); M0 if the relevant reaction is never set to zero; DM1 solve; A1 3.5 (MS p.10)

parts.ask: F has magnitude 8 N on bearing 240°, G has magnitude 10 N due south; R = F + G: find |R|
parts.ms: M1 equation in R only (cosine rule with 120°, or components); M0 for cosine rule with 60° or misquoted rule; A1 correct; A1 √244, 16 or better (MS p.11)

parts.ask: Find the direction of R as a bearing to the nearest degree
parts.ms: M1 equation in a relevant angle using their R (sine rule, cosine rule or components); A1 correct; A1 relevant angle (26.3° or 33.67°) to nearest degree; A1 206° cao (MS p.11)

parts.ask: Agatha at (11i + 11j) m with velocity (3i − j) m/s: find her position vector at time t
parts.ms: M1A1 (MS p.12)

parts.ask: Agatha passes P at t = 6; Brionie starts at (7i + 16j) with velocity (4i − 2j): show Brionie also passes through P and find when
parts.ms: M1 r_A at t = 6 = 29i + 5j; M1 equate r_B = (7i + 16j) + t(4i − 2j) to it; DM1 solve both components explicitly to get t = 5.5 twice (dividing vectors is DM0; one ratio equation not enough); A1* (MS pp.12–13)

parts.ask: Show that AB = [(t − 4)i + (5 − t)j] m
parts.final_form: printed result, not as a column vector
parts.ms: M1 r_B − r_A (M0 if starting from r_A = r_B); A1* given answer with the difference written out in full before simplifying (MS pp.12–13)

parts.ask: Find the distance between the girls when closest
parts.ms: M1 AB² = (t − 4)² + (5 − t)²; A1 2(t − 4.5)² + 0.5 (or derivative 4t − 18, or discriminant); M1 complete method for the minimum; A1 √0.5 = 0.71 (MS pp.12–13)

parts.ask: Parachutist falls freely from rest for 2.5 s: find his speed when the parachute opens
He then decelerates at 3.9 m/s² for T s to speed V, then constant until landing at t = 20: sketch the speed-time graph
parts.final_form: three-stage graph with 24.5, V, 2.5, 2.5 + T, 20 marked
parts.ms: B1 shape, second line less steep than the first (may be reflected; B0 for solid vertical line at t = 20); B1 all five values placed (MS p.14)

parts.ask: He falls 73.75 m while decelerating (T < 6): find T
parts.ms: M1 equation in T only with correct structure, e.g. 73.75 = 24.5T − ½(3.9)T²; A1A1M1(A1) correct equation(s), −1 each error; A1 5, single answer with the other root clearly rejected (MS p.14)

parts.ask: Find, to the nearest metre, the height of H above the ground
parts.ms: M1 total area under the graph (triangle + trapezium + rectangle); A2 correct, −1 each error: ½×24.5×2.5 + 73.75 + 12.5 × (24.5 − 3.9×5); A1 167 (MS p.14)

parts.ask: A (2 kg) on a rough plane (tan α = 3/4, μ = 1/4) joined over a smooth pulley at the top to B (4 kg) hanging h m above the ground; released, B descends: find the tension
parts.ms: M1A1 R = 2g cos α; M1A1 for A: T − 2g sin α − F = 2a; M1A1 for B: 4g − T = 4a (either may be the whole-system equation); B1 F = 0.25R; M1 solve for T (two equations of motion with a); A1 12g/5 = 24 or 23.5 (MS pp.15–16)

parts.ask: B stops on hitting the ground; A comes to rest before reaching the pulley: find, in terms of h, the range of d
parts.ms: M1 eliminate T to find a; A1 a = 0.4g (must be used in (b)); M1 v² = 2(0.4g)h = 4gh/5 (M0 if 0.4g/g not found properly); B1 new equation of motion for A: −6g/5 − 2g/5 = 2a′; M1 0 = 4gh/5 − (8g/5)s; A1 s = ½h; A1 d > 1.5h (MS pp.15–16)

parts.ask: State one physical factor, other than air resistance, that would make the model more realistic
parts.final_form: e.g. weight of string, extensibility, friction at the pulley
parts.ms: B1 any correct factor; simply restating the question is B0; B0 with incorrect extras (MS pp.15–16)

parts.ask: P (3m, speed ku) and Q (5m, speed 2u) collide head-on on a smooth surface; afterwards P has speed u, Q speed 3u with direction reversed: find the magnitude of the impulse on Q
parts.ms: M1 I = m(v − u) for Q with correct terms, condone sign errors, M0 if g included; A1 25mu, must be positive (MS p.8)

parts.ask: Find the two possible values of k
parts.ms: M1 CLM (or equal and opposite impulses), dimensionally correct; A1 correct equation for either case, e.g. 3mku − 10mu = ±3mu + 15mu; A1 one value; M1 second equation with P's final direction reversed; A1 second value (MS p.8)

parts.ask: Car with constant acceleration a passes A at u m/s; travels 20 m in the first 3 s and 10 m in the fourth second; speed at B is 20 m/s: find the time from A to B
parts.ms: M1A1 s = ut + ½at² for the first 3 s (20 = 3u + 9a/2); M1A1 second equation (10 = (u + 3a) + a/2, or 30 = 4u + 8a); M1 solve; A1 u = 25/6, a = 5/3 (1.7, 4.2 or better); M1 v = u + at with 20; A1 9.5 cao (MS p.9)

parts.ask: F1 = (5i + 2j), F2 = (−3i + j), F3 = (ai + bj) N on a 4 kg particle in equilibrium on a smooth horizontal surface: find the angle between F3 and −j
parts.ms: M1 equilibrium sum = 0 to find F3; A1 F3 = −2i − 3j; M1 equation in a relevant angle (tan θ = 2/3); A1 33.7° (MS p.10)

parts.ask: F3 replaced by F4 = λ(i + 3j) N (λ > 0); acceleration has magnitude 3.25 m/s²: find λ
parts.ms: B1 resultant (2 + λ)i + (3 + 3λ)j; M1 F = 4a with their resultant (all three forces added); M1 magnitude of a or F; M1 use 3.25 or 13 to form a 3-term quadratic (10λ² + 22λ − 156 = 0); A1 λ = 3, A0 if two values given (MS p.10)

parts.ms: M1 T − 40g = 40 × 0.2, all terms, in T only; A1 correct; A1 400, positive (MS p.11)

parts.ask: With a 12 kg box of tools, the bucket moves down with deceleration 0.1 m/s²: find the normal reaction between bucket and box
parts.ms: M1 equation for the box only, all terms: 12g − R = −0.1 × 12; A1 correct; A1 119 or 120, positive (MS p.11)

parts.ask: Constant acceleration: velocity (3i + 5j) km/h at 2 pm and (i + 7j) at 2.30 pm; at time T hours after 2 pm P moves in the direction −i + 2j: find T
parts.ms: M1 a = (v − u)/0.5; A1 a = −4i + 4j; M1 v_P = (3i + 5j) + t(−4i + 4j); A1ft collected (3 − 4t)i + (5 + 4t)j; M1 correct ratio equation 5 + 4T = −2(3 − 4T); A1 11/4 (MS p.12)

parts.ask: Q has velocity (−4 − 2t)i + (μ + 3t)j; at some instant v_P = v_Q: find μ
parts.ms: M1 equate i and j coefficients (3 − 4t = −4 − 2t, 5 + 4t = μ + 3t); M1 solve for μ; A1 8.5 (MS p.12)

parts.ask: Rough plane at θ (tan θ = 5/12), μ = 1/4; particle of 6 kg projected up the slope at 5 m/s: find the friction while it moves up
parts.ms: M1 resolve perpendicular (sin/cos confusion condoned); A1 R = 6g cos θ; A1 F = R/4 = 18g/13, 13.6 or 14 (MS p.13)

parts.ask: It comes to instantaneous rest at B: find AB
parts.ms: M1A1 equation of motion up the plane −F − 6g sin θ = 6a; M1 suvat with their a (a ≠ g) to find s; A1 0 = 5² − 2(8g/13)s; A1 2.07 or 2.1, positive (MS p.13)

parts.ask: It slides back down; at C its speed is again 5 m/s: find BC
parts.ms: M1A1 equation of motion down the plane 6g sin θ − F = 6a′; M1 suvat with a′ ≠ a, a′ ≠ g; A1 5² = 2(2g/13)s; A1 8.29 or 8.3 (MS p.13)

parts.ms: M1A1, M1A1 two equations using R and 3R (e.g. 4R = 60g; M(A): 60gx = Ra + 3R × 6a); consistent omission of g can score full marks; SC M(G) M2A2; A1 19a/4 (MS p.14)

parts.ask: Box M kg placed at E (AE = 2a); the reactions at C and D are now equal: find M
parts.ms: M1A1ft, M1A1ft two equations in M and S with x substituted (e.g. 60g + Mg = 2S; M(C): 60g(x − a) + Mga = 5aS); A1 50 exact (MS p.14)

parts.ask: Tram A accelerates at 2 m/s² for 5 s then constant speed; tram B starts at t = 20, accelerates at 3 m/s² for 4 s then constant: sketch both speed-time graphs on the same axes until B overtakes A
parts.final_form: both graphs on one set of axes; 5, 20, 24 marked
parts.ms: B1 A's shape from the origin (B0 if solid vertical line at the end); B1 B's shape, later start, steeper, crossing A, same end; DB1 5, 20, 24 shown (MS p.15)

parts.ask: When the trams have the same speed, A is d m ahead of B: find d
parts.ms: B1 t = 70/3 (B reaches 10 m/s); M1 distance for one tram; A1 correct; M1 second distance and subtract; A1 575/3 (MS p.15)

parts.ask: Find the distance from the depot when B overtakes A
parts.ms: M1 equate the two distances at time t with correct structure; A2 correct unsimplified equation, −1 each error, e.g. ½×5×10 + 10(t − 5) = ½×4×12 + 12(t − 24); M1 solve, t = 119.5; A1 1170 (MS p.15)

parts.ms: M1A1 first equation in d, R, M (e.g. vertical R + 2R = Mg, or moments); M1A1 second equation (e.g. M(C): 2R × 4.5 = Mg(d − 2.5)); SC M(G) alone M2A2,1,0; DM1 solve for numerical d; A1 5.5. Consistent omission of g allowed; R and 2R reversed consistently: apply scheme (MS p.6)

parts.ms: M1 CLM 2m×3u = 2mv + 4m×2u (or impulses equated), condone sign errors; A1 correct; A1 v = −u so speed u, must be positive (MS p.7)

parts.ask: State clearly the direction of motion of P after the collision
parts.ms: DB1 opposite to original direction, reversed, direction QP; "direction changed" is B0; depends on ±u in (a) (MS p.7)

parts.ask: Q comes to rest after travelling 6u²/g along the plane; coefficient of friction μ: find μ
parts.ms: B1 R = 4mg; M1 equation of motion F = 4ma (or impulse-momentum −Ft = 4m(0 − 2u)); A1 with F = μ·4mg; M1A1 suvat 0² = (2u)² − 2a(6u²/g) (or distance-time); A1 1/3 correctly obtained; equations must be consistent for both A marks (MS p.7)

parts.ask: Car at 25 m/s; sign 48 m ahead of A; first model: uniform deceleration 6 m/s² from A to the sign: find the speed at the sign
Second model: decelerate at 6 m/s² to 13 m/s then constant speed to the sign: find t at the sign
parts.ms: M1 time to 13 m/s = 2 s; M1 distance in that time = 38 m; DM1 total time 2 + (48 − 38)/13; A1 36/13 (2.8 or better) (MS p.8)

parts.ask: Third model: constant 25 m/s until t = 0.2 (reaction time), then decelerate at 6 m/s² to 13 m/s, then constant: find t at the sign
parts.ms: M1 deceleration time 2 s (may be implied by 2.2); M1 distance 0.2×25 + 38 = 43; DM1 total time 0.2 + 2 + (48 − 43)/13; A1 168/65 (2.6 or better) (MS p.8)

parts.ask: r = (t − 3)i + (1 − 2t)j: find, to the nearest degree, the angle between r and j when t = 2
parts.ms: B1 r = −i − 3j; M1 trig ratio of a relevant angle (tan = ±1/3 or ±3, or scalar product); A1 162° or 198° (MS p.9)

parts.ask: Find the values of t for which P is 2.5 m from O
parts.ms: M1 (t − 3)² + (1 − 2t)² = 2.5²; DM1 simplify to a 3-term quadratic; A1 4t² − 8t + 3 = 0; M(A)1 t = 0.5; A1 t = 1.5 (MS p.9)

parts.ask: Bead 0.2 kg on a fixed rough vertical wire, pushed by a light rod PQ at α to the wire (tan α = 4/3) with thrust T: find the magnitude and direction of the friction when T = 2.5
parts.ms: M1 resolve vertically ±F = 0.2g − 2.5cos α (μR allowed for F); A1 correct; A1 0.46 N upwards — both magnitude (positive) and direction needed (MS p.10)

parts.ask: Greatest possible value of T is 6.125: find μ
parts.ms: M1A1 vertical: F + 0.2g = 6.125cos α (M0 if T = 2.5 used); M1A1 horizontal: R = 6.125 sin α (= 4.9); B1 F = μR (B0 if R from (a)); DM1 solve; A1 0.35. F and R interchanged: max B1 (MS p.10)

parts.ms: M1 0 = u − 9.8×2.5 or gradient of the graph (g or 9.81 allowed for M); A1 24.5 or 25, positive; g = 9.81 penalised once in the question (MS p.11)

parts.ask: Find the height of A above the ground
parts.ms: M1 complete method for the final displacement, e.g. s = 24.5×7 − ½×9.8×7² or graph areas; A1ft on their u; A1 68.6 or 69 (MS p.11)

parts.ask: A (2m) on a rough plane (tan α = 3/4, μ = 1/2) joined over a smooth light pulley at the top to B (3m) hanging; A moves up: write equations of motion for (i) A and (ii) B
parts.ms: M1A1 for A: T − 2mg sin α − F = 2ma; M1A1 for B: 3mg − T = 3ma; labels (i)/(ii) ignored; −a in both allowed (MS p.12)

parts.ask: Find, in terms of g, the acceleration of A
parts.ms: M1A1 R = 2mg cos α; B1 F = ½R; DM1 substitute trig and solve the two equations (or whole-system equation); A1 g/5 (MS p.12)

parts.ask: Find the magnitude of the force exerted on the pulley by the string
parts.ms: DM1 find T = 12mg/5 (23.52m); M1 correct expression in T and α, e.g. 2T cos((90° − α)/2) or cosine rule with 90° + α; DM1 substitute T and trig; A1 48√5mg/25, 4.3mg or better (MS p.12)

parts.ask: State how you used the information that the pulley is smooth
parts.final_form: tension same on both sides of the pulley
parts.ms: B1 tension is the same on either side of the pulley; B0 for "same for A and B"/"same for both strings" or incorrect extras (MS p.12)

parts.ask: Ship leaves port (−2i + 9j) km at 7 am; at 7.36 am it is at (4i + 6j) km: show its velocity is (10i − 5j) km/h
parts.final_form: printed result in i, j form
parts.ms: M1 (4i + 6j) = (−2i + 9j) + 0.6v; A1* one more line of working and answer in i–j form; verification allowed (MS p.13)

parts.ask: Find the position vector of the ship t hours after leaving port
parts.ms: M1 correct structure; A1 (MS p.13)

parts.ask: At 8.48 am a lighthouse is due east of the ship; at 9 am it is north-east: find the position vector of the lighthouse
parts.ms: M1 r at t = 1.8; A1 16i; M1 r at t = 2 (= 18i − j); A1 lighthouse 19i (MS p.13)

parts.ask: Find the position vector of the ship when it is due south of the lighthouse
parts.ms: M1 equate i-components −2 + 10t = 19; A1 t = 2.1; DM1 substitute; A1 19i − 1.5j (MS p.13)

parts.ask: Particle of weight 5 N on a string from O, held in equilibrium by a force F perpendicular to the string; string at 60° to the vertical: find F
parts.ms: M1 complete method to an equation in F only (resolve perpendicular to the string, triangle of forces or Lami); if resolving H and V, T must be eliminated; M0 for wrong angles such as 45°; A1 F = 5cos 30°; A1 4.33… (using a wrong T from (b) first: M1A0A0) (MS p.7)

parts.ask: Find the tension in the string
parts.ms: M1 equation in T only (resolve along the string etc.); A1 T = 5 sin 30°; A1 5/2 (using a wrong F from (a): M1A0A0) (MS p.7)

sources.qp: github:RayZ3R0/papernexus-finder@921bdf4f papers/mathematics/qp/mech1/2022/Mathematics MECH1 (IAL) - January 2022 - QP (WME01).pdf (PMT-stamped Pearson PDF, WME01/01, P68783A, 28 pp.; copy local:src/WME01/2022-01_01_qp.pdf)

parts.ask: P (mass km, speed 3u) and Q (mass m, speed u) collide head-on; each reverses direction with speed halved: find k
parts.ms: M1 CLM, correct number of terms, condone sign errors, consistent cancelled m or extra g allowed; A1 equation with one error; A1 correct: 3kmu − mu = −(3/2)kmu + (1/2)mu; A1 1/3 (MS p.8)

parts.ask: Find, in terms of m and u, the magnitude of the impulse on Q
parts.ms: M1 difference of momenta with masses and speeds paired correctly (k need not be substituted; M0 if g included); A1 ±m(u/2 − (−u)) or via P; A1 3mu/2, must be positive (MS p.8)

sources.qp: github:RayZ3R0/papernexus-finder@921bdf4f papers/mathematics/qp/mech1/2022/Mathematics MECH1 (IAL) - January 2022 - QP (WME01).pdf (PMT-stamped Pearson PDF, WME01/01, P68783A, 28 pp.; copy local:src/WME01/2022-01_01_qp.pdf)

parts.ask: Uniform beam ADCB, 5 m, on a step with edge D (DB = 1.3 m); boy of 30 kg at C (CB = 0.5 m) puts it on the point of tilting: find the mass of the beam
parts.ms: M1 equation in m only with the reaction at D (M0 if reaction not at D; other points need the reaction eliminated); A1 M(D): mg × 1.2 = 30g × 0.8; A1 20 (MS p.9)

parts.ask: A block X kg is placed at A: find the smallest X so that the boy can stand at B without tilting
parts.ms: M1 equation (or correct-way inequality) in X only; A1ft M(D): Xg × 3.7 + 20g × 1.2 = 30g × 1.3, ft their 20; A1 150/37, 4.1 or better (MS p.9)

parts.ask: State how the modelling assumption that the block is a particle was used
parts.final_form: its weight acts at a point (A)
parts.ms: B1 mass/weight of the block concentrated (acts) at a point; must mention mass or weight and "acting/concentrated at a point" (MS p.9)

sources.qp: github:RayZ3R0/papernexus-finder@921bdf4f papers/mathematics/qp/mech1/2022/Mathematics MECH1 (IAL) - January 2022 - QP (WME01).pdf (PMT-stamped Pearson PDF, WME01/01, P68783A, 28 pp.; copy local:src/WME01/2022-01_01_qp.pdf)

parts.ask: Ball projected vertically up from A, 24.5 m above the ground; it first comes to rest at B with AB = 19.6 m and hits the ground at t = T: find T
parts.ms: M1A1 0² = u² − 2g(19.6) (u = 19.6); M1A1 second equation using 24.5 or 44.1, e.g. −24.5 = uT − ½gT²; DM1 equation in T only and solve (not if it has no solutions); A1 T = 5 (A0 if g = 9.8 not used) (MS p.10)

parts.ask: Sketch the speed-time graph from t = 0 to T (no further calculation needed)
parts.final_form: V-shape starting on the speed axis, touching the t-axis
parts.ms: B1 V shape only, starting on the speed axis with a point on the t-axis; DB1 roughly equal angles, second line longer, T marked; reflected graph B0 DB0 (MS p.10)

sources.qp: github:RayZ3R0/papernexus-finder@921bdf4f papers/mathematics/qp/mech1/2022/Mathematics MECH1 (IAL) - January 2022 - QP (WME01).pdf (PMT-stamped Pearson PDF, WME01/01, P68783A, 28 pp.; copy local:src/WME01/2022-01_01_qp.pdf)

parts.ask: Particle of mass m on a rough plane (tan α = 3/4) held by a force X up the slope; with X = 2P it is about to slide up, with X = P about to slide down: find μ
parts.ms: M1A1 R = mg cos α; M1 resolve parallel; A1 mg sin α + F = 2P; A1 mg sin α − F = P (A0 if different R or F used); M1 F = μR; M1 substitute trig, eliminate P and F, solve; A1 0.25. Omitting g consistently max M1A0M1A0A0M1M1A1; using cos(4/5) for cos α is an A error (MS p.11)

sources.qp: github:RayZ3R0/papernexus-finder@921bdf4f papers/mathematics/qp/mech1/2022/Mathematics MECH1 (IAL) - January 2022 - QP (WME01).pdf (PMT-stamped Pearson PDF, WME01/01, P68783A, 28 pp.; copy local:src/WME01/2022-01_01_qp.pdf)

parts.ask: Particle of mass 2 kg under forces (pi + qj) N and (2qi + pj) N has acceleration (i − j) m/s²: find p and q
parts.ms: M1 F = ma with m = 2, adding the forces; M1 equate coefficients to an equation in p and q only (a ratio without equating is M0); A1 p + 2q = 2; A1 q + p = −2; A1 both (MS p.12)

parts.ask: Find the angle between the direction of the acceleration and j
parts.ms: M1 trig for a relevant angle (tan = ±1); A1 135° or equivalent, degrees or radians (MS p.12)

parts.ask: At t = 0, v = (3i − 4j) m/s; at t = T, P moves in the direction 11i − 13j: find T
parts.ms: M1 v = (3i − 4j) + T(i − j); M1 ratio of components with their v, correct way up; A1 (3 + T)/(−4 − T) = 11/(−13); DM1 solve; A1 2.5 (MS p.12)

sources.qp: github:RayZ3R0/papernexus-finder@921bdf4f papers/mathematics/qp/mech1/2022/Mathematics MECH1 (IAL) - January 2022 - QP (WME01).pdf (PMT-stamped Pearson PDF, WME01/01, P68783A, 28 pp.; copy local:src/WME01/2022-01_01_qp.pdf)
sources.ms: github:RayZ3R0/papernexus-finder@921bdf4f papers/mathematics/ms/mech1/2022/Mathematics MECH1 (IAL) - January 2022 - MS (WME01).pdf (Mark Scheme (Results) January 2022, WME01_01_2201_MS, log P68783A, 15 pp.; copy local:src/WME01/2022-01_01_ms.pdf)

parts.ask: P (4m) on a rough plane (tan α = 3/4, μ = 1/4) joined over a smooth pulley at the top to Q (m) on a smooth horizontal plane; P moves down: write down an equation of motion for Q
parts.ms: B1 T = ma (allow −a), must appear in (a) (MS p.13)

parts.ask: Find, in terms of m and g, the tension in the string
parts.ms: M1A1 equation of motion for P along the plane, 4mg sin α − T − F = 4ma (or whole system 4mg sin α − F = 5ma); B1 F = (1/4)R; M1A1 R = 4mg cos α; DM1 solve for T as kmg; A1 8mg/25 (MS p.13)

parts.ask: Find the magnitude of the force exerted on the pulley by the string
parts.ms: M1A1 expression in T and α, e.g. 2T sin(α/2), cosine rule or components (correct angle needed); M1 substitute T (form kmg) and trig; A1 8√10mg/125, 2m, 1.98m or 0.2mg or better (MS p.13)

parts.ask: State where you used the information that the string is light
parts.final_form: tension the same throughout the string (each section)
parts.ms: B1 e.g. tension is the same throughout a section of the string; "tension is the same throughout the string" alone is B0 per the scheme note; B0 with incorrect extras (MS p.13)

sources.qp: github:RayZ3R0/papernexus-finder@921bdf4f papers/mathematics/qp/mech1/2022/Mathematics MECH1 (IAL) - January 2022 - QP (WME01).pdf (PMT-stamped Pearson PDF, WME01/01, P68783A, 28 pp.; copy local:src/WME01/2022-01_01_qp.pdf)
sources.ms: github:RayZ3R0/papernexus-finder@921bdf4f papers/mathematics/ms/mech1/2022/Mathematics MECH1 (IAL) - January 2022 - MS (WME01).pdf (Mark Scheme (Results) January 2022, WME01_01_2201_MS, log P68783A, 15 pp.; copy local:src/WME01/2022-01_01_ms.pdf)

parts.ask: Ship A: velocity (3i − 10j) km/h, at t = 0 at (13i + 5j) km: find r in terms of t
parts.ms: M1 correct structure; A1 (MS p.14)

parts.ask: Ship B: velocity (15i + 14j), at t = 0 at (3i − 5j): show AB = [(12t − 10)i + (24t − 10)j] km
parts.ms: M1A1 s = (3i − 5j) + t(15i + 14j); M1 AB = s − r (either order for M); A1* given answer correctly obtained; −(10 + 12t)i + … form is A0 (MS p.14)

parts.ask: Find the shortest distance between the ships
parts.ms: M1 |AB|² = (12t − 10)² + (24t − 10)² = 720t² − 720t + 200; M1 differentiate, complete the square or t = −b/2a; A1 correct equation/expression; DM1 critical t = ½; M1 substitute non-zero t into |AB| with square root; A1 √20, 4.5 or better. Discriminant method alternative (MS pp.14–15)

parts.ask: Find the bearing of B from A when they are closest
parts.ms: M1 AB = −4i + 2j at t = ½ and a relevant angle (e.g. 26.56°); A1 297° or better (MS pp.14–15)

sources.qp: github:RayZ3R0/papernexus-finder@921bdf4f papers/mathematics/qp/mech1/2022/Mathematics MECH1 (IAL) - January 2022 - QP (WME01).pdf (PMT-stamped Pearson PDF, WME01/01, P68783A, 28 pp.; copy local:src/WME01/2022-01_01_qp.pdf)
sources.ms: github:RayZ3R0/papernexus-finder@921bdf4f papers/mathematics/ms/mech1/2022/Mathematics MECH1 (IAL) - January 2022 - MS (WME01).pdf (Mark Scheme (Results) January 2022, WME01_01_2201_MS, log P68783A, 15 pp.; copy local:src/WME01/2022-01_01_ms.pdf)

parts.ask: P and Q (mass 3m, speed 2u) collide directly while moving towards each other; impulse of P on Q has magnitude 4mu: find the speed of Q after the collision
parts.ms: M1 impulse-momentum equation for Q, difference of momenta, condone sign errors (m for 3m allowed), e.g. −4mu = 3m(v − 2u); A1 correct equation; A1 2u/3, must be positive (MS p.7)

parts.ask: State the direction of motion of Q after the collision
parts.ms: DB1 "same as its original direction"/"unchanged"/"towards P"; depends on v = ±2u/3 in (a); "motion of Q is unchanged" is B0 (MS p.7)

sources.qp: github:RayZ3R0/papernexus-finder@921bdf4f papers/mathematics/qp/mech1/2022/Mathematics MECH1 (IAL) - May 2022 - QP (WME01).pdf (PMT-stamped Pearson PDF, WME01/01, P71403A, 28 pp.; copy local:src/WME01/2022-06_01_qp.pdf)
sources.ms: github:RayZ3R0/papernexus-finder@921bdf4f papers/mathematics/ms/mech1/2022/Mathematics MECH1 (IAL) - May 2022 - MS (WME01).pdf (Mark Scheme (Results) Summer 2022, WME01_01_2206_MS, log P71403A, 19 pp.; copy local:src/WME01/2022-06_01_ms.pdf)

parts.ask: Motorbike with constant acceleration passes P, then Q 10 s later at 28 m/s; PQ = 220 m: find the acceleration
parts.ms: M1 complete method to an equation in a only, e.g. s = vt − ½at²: 220 = 280 − 50a (incorrect suvat is M0; M0 if u = 0 assumed); A1 correct; A1 1.2 (using s = ut + ½at² "reversed" gives −1.2: M1A0A0 unless corrected) (MS pp.8–9)

parts.ask: Find the distance travelled during the fifth second after passing P
parts.ms: M1A1ft speed or distance at t = 4 or 5 (u = 16; e.g. s₄ = 73.6, s₅ = 95), ft only if u was used in (a); M1 complete method for the required distance (s₅ − s₄ etc.); A1 21.4 (MS pp.8–9)

sources.qp: github:RayZ3R0/papernexus-finder@921bdf4f papers/mathematics/qp/mech1/2022/Mathematics MECH1 (IAL) - May 2022 - QP (WME01).pdf (PMT-stamped Pearson PDF, WME01/01, P71403A, 28 pp.; copy local:src/WME01/2022-06_01_qp.pdf)
sources.ms: github:RayZ3R0/papernexus-finder@921bdf4f papers/mathematics/ms/mech1/2022/Mathematics MECH1 (IAL) - May 2022 - MS (WME01).pdf (Mark Scheme (Results) Summer 2022, WME01_01_2206_MS, log P71403A, 19 pp.; copy local:src/WME01/2022-06_01_ms.pdf)

parts.ask: Tractor 6 t drags a block 2 t by a light inextensible horizontal cable; driving force 7400 N, tractor resistance 200 N, block resistance R N; tension 6000 N and accelerating: find R
parts.ms: M1A1, M1A1 any two of: tractor 7400 − 200 − 6000 = 6000a; whole 7400 − 200 − R = 8000a; block 6000 − R = 2000a (6000 N must be used as the tension for an M mark); DM1 solve for R; A1 5600; using tonnes consistently is a misread, max M1A0M1A0M1A1 (MS p.10)

parts.ask: State how you have used the fact that the cable is modelled as inextensible
parts.ms: B1 tractor and block (both) have the same acceleration; just "same acceleration" is not enough without "both"/naming them; B0 with extra wrong answers (MS p.10)

sources.qp: github:RayZ3R0/papernexus-finder@921bdf4f papers/mathematics/qp/mech1/2022/Mathematics MECH1 (IAL) - May 2022 - QP (WME01).pdf (PMT-stamped Pearson PDF, WME01/01, P71403A, 28 pp.; copy local:src/WME01/2022-06_01_qp.pdf)
sources.ms: github:RayZ3R0/papernexus-finder@921bdf4f papers/mathematics/ms/mech1/2022/Mathematics MECH1 (IAL) - May 2022 - MS (WME01).pdf (Mark Scheme (Results) Summer 2022, WME01_01_2206_MS, log P71403A, 19 pp.; copy local:src/WME01/2022-06_01_ms.pdf)

parts.ask: Block 5 kg at rest on rough horizontal plane, μ = 3/7; force P = 14 N at 30° above the horizontal: find the friction and describe what happens, justifying
parts.final_form: friction 12.1 N (12 or better); block does not move
parts.ms: M1A1 R = 5g − 14 sin 30°; A1 R = 42; M1 max friction = (3/7)(42) = 18; M1 compare horizontal component 14cos 30° = 12.12… with the maximum friction — "maximum" must be stated, M0 if friction is said to be 18 N; A1 friction 12 or better and block remains at rest (MS p.11)

parts.ask: P is changed so the block is on the point of slipping: find P
parts.ms: M1A1 resolve vertically P sin 30° + S = 5g; M1A1 horizontally P cos 30° = (3/7)S (using the max friction from (a) or wrong S is M1A0); DM1 solve two equations; A1 19 or 19.4 (MS p.11)

sources.qp: github:RayZ3R0/papernexus-finder@921bdf4f papers/mathematics/qp/mech1/2022/Mathematics MECH1 (IAL) - May 2022 - QP (WME01).pdf (PMT-stamped Pearson PDF, WME01/01, P71403A, 28 pp.; copy local:src/WME01/2022-06_01_qp.pdf)
sources.ms: github:RayZ3R0/papernexus-finder@921bdf4f papers/mathematics/ms/mech1/2022/Mathematics MECH1 (IAL) - May 2022 - MS (WME01).pdf (Mark Scheme (Results) Summer 2022, WME01_01_2206_MS, log P71403A, 19 pp.; copy local:src/WME01/2022-06_01_ms.pdf)

parts.ask: Uniform rod AB, 5 m, 5 kg, on supports C and D (AC = 1 m, DB = 2 m); 10 kg at A and M kg at B: find, in terms of M, the reaction at C
parts.ms: M1 complete method to an equation in R_C and M only (M0 if reactions assumed equal), e.g. M(D): 2R_C + 2Mg = 0.5×5g + 3×10g; A1 correct; A1 expression with g collected (MS pp.12–13)

parts.ask: Find, in terms of M, the reaction at D
parts.ms: M1 equation in R_D and M only, e.g. M(C): 2R_D + 10g = 1.5×5g + 4Mg; A1 correct; A1 expression (MS pp.12–13)

parts.ask: Hence, or otherwise, find the range of possible values of M
parts.ms: M1 use R_C ≥ 0 or R_D ≥ 0 (equality or > allowed); A1ft one critical value, must be positive; A1 0.625 ≤ M ≤ 16.25 (2 s.f. or better); over-accuracy after g = 9.8 penalised once in the question (MS pp.12–13)

sources.qp: github:RayZ3R0/papernexus-finder@921bdf4f papers/mathematics/qp/mech1/2022/Mathematics MECH1 (IAL) - May 2022 - QP (WME01).pdf (PMT-stamped Pearson PDF, WME01/01, P71403A, 28 pp.; copy local:src/WME01/2022-06_01_qp.pdf)
sources.ms: github:RayZ3R0/papernexus-finder@921bdf4f papers/mathematics/ms/mech1/2022/Mathematics MECH1 (IAL) - May 2022 - MS (WME01).pdf (Mark Scheme (Results) Summer 2022, WME01_01_2206_MS, log P71403A, 19 pp.; copy local:src/WME01/2022-06_01_ms.pdf)

parts.ask: Constant acceleration: velocity (−i + 4j) m/s at t = 1 and (5i − 8j) m/s at t = 4: find the speed at t = 3.5 s
parts.ms: M1A1 v = u + at with t = 3 to find a = 2i − 4j (u, v reversed allowed); M1 v at t = 3.5 using t = 2.5 from t = 1 (M0 if u = 0 assumed); A1 4i − 6j; M1 Pythagoras with square root; A1 √52 = 7.2 or better. Ratio method alternative M2A1A1M1A1 (MS p.14)

sources.qp: github:RayZ3R0/papernexus-finder@921bdf4f papers/mathematics/qp/mech1/2022/Mathematics MECH1 (IAL) - May 2022 - QP (WME01).pdf (PMT-stamped Pearson PDF, WME01/01, P71403A, 28 pp.; copy local:src/WME01/2022-06_01_qp.pdf)
sources.ms: github:RayZ3R0/papernexus-finder@921bdf4f papers/mathematics/ms/mech1/2022/Mathematics MECH1 (IAL) - May 2022 - MS (WME01).pdf (Mark Scheme (Results) Summer 2022, WME01_01_2206_MS, log P71403A, 19 pp.; copy local:src/WME01/2022-06_01_ms.pdf)

parts.ask: 100 m race: Ajaz accelerates at 0.8 m/s² to 4 m/s then constant; Beth accelerates at 1 m/s² for T s then constant; they finish together: sketch both speed-time graphs on the same axes
parts.final_form: two trapezium-shaped graphs ending at the same time; 4 and T marked
parts.ms: B1 Ajaz shape; B1 Beth steeper initially, crossing Ajaz's graph, same end time (solid vertical end line B0 once); B1 4 and T marked; separate axes max B1B0B1 (MS pp.15–16)

parts.ask: Find the time taken by Ajaz to complete the race
parts.ms: B1 5 s to reach 4 m/s; M1 area/distance equation = 100 with correct structure (trapezium or rectangle ± triangle), single suvat for whole motion M0; A1ft on their 5; A1 27.5 (MS pp.15–16)

parts.ask: Find the value of T
parts.ms: M1 area equation in T only = 100, correct structure; A1ft on their 27.5; A1 T² − 55T + 200 = 0; A1 3.9 or better (MS pp.15–16)

parts.ask: Find the difference in their speeds as they cross the line
parts.ms: M1 4 − T (or T − 4); A1ft on T < 4, at least 2 s.f. (MS pp.15–16)

sources.qp: github:RayZ3R0/papernexus-finder@921bdf4f papers/mathematics/qp/mech1/2022/Mathematics MECH1 (IAL) - May 2022 - QP (WME01).pdf (PMT-stamped Pearson PDF, WME01/01, P71403A, 28 pp.; copy local:src/WME01/2022-06_01_qp.pdf)
sources.ms: github:RayZ3R0/papernexus-finder@921bdf4f papers/mathematics/ms/mech1/2022/Mathematics MECH1 (IAL) - May 2022 - MS (WME01).pdf (Mark Scheme (Results) Summer 2022, WME01_01_2206_MS, log P71403A, 19 pp.; copy local:src/WME01/2022-06_01_ms.pdf)

parts.ask: Boat Q has velocity (20i − 20j) m/s (i east, j north): find its direction of travel as a bearing
parts.ms: M1 trig/isosceles triangle using Q's velocity (M0 otherwise); A1 135° (MS p.17)

parts.ask: P (velocity 15i) starts at O, Q at 200j m: show PQ = [5ti + (200 − 20t)j] m
parts.ms: M1A1 p = 15ti; A1 q = 200j + t(20i − 20j); M1 PQ = q − p (M0 if p = q), this line must be seen; A1* given answer correctly obtained, vector form required for the answer (MS p.17)

parts.ask: Find the bearing of P from Q when t = 10
parts.ms: M1 PQ = 50i at t = 10 (or p and q at t = 10; may be implied by a diagram); A1 270° (MS p.17)

parts.ask: Find the distance between P and Q when Q is north-east of P
parts.ms: M1 equate components 5t = 200 − 20t (no vectors); A1 t = 8; M1 substitute into PQ; M1 magnitude with square root; A1 40√2, 57 or better (MS pp.17–18)

parts.ask: Find the times when P and Q are 200 m apart
parts.final_form: t = 0 and t = 320/17 ≈ 18.8 s (19 or better)
parts.ms: M1 Pythagoras to an equation in t; A1 425t² − 8000t = 0; A1 both answers (isw) (MS pp.17–18)

sources.qp: github:RayZ3R0/papernexus-finder@921bdf4f papers/mathematics/qp/mech1/2022/Mathematics MECH1 (IAL) - May 2022 - QP (WME01).pdf (PMT-stamped Pearson PDF, WME01/01, P71403A, 28 pp.; copy local:src/WME01/2022-06_01_qp.pdf)
sources.ms: github:RayZ3R0/papernexus-finder@921bdf4f papers/mathematics/ms/mech1/2022/Mathematics MECH1 (IAL) - May 2022 - MS (WME01).pdf (Mark Scheme (Results) Summer 2022, WME01_01_2206_MS, log P71403A, 19 pp.; copy local:src/WME01/2022-06_01_ms.pdf)

parts.ask: Truck S (20 t) at 4 m/s hits truck T (30 t) at rest; they couple: find the common speed after the collision
parts.ms: M1 CLM equation, condone sign errors/extra g, any consistent mass ratio (2×4 = 5v etc.) or equating impulses; A1 1.6, units not needed but must be positive (MS p.7)
parts.er: Well answered via CLM for the whole system; common errors were signs and wrong mass ratios; the speed must be given as positive (ER p.3)

parts.ask: Find the magnitude of the impulse exerted on S, stating the units
parts.ms: M1 impulse = difference of momenta for one truck, condone sign errors (masses 20 or 30 allowed; M0 if g included or mass omitted); A1ft correct equation on their v (for S, 4 and v must have opposite signs); A1 cao 48000 N s or 48 kN s, units needed (kg m s⁻¹ allowed), positive (MS p.7)
parts.er: Most applied impulse-momentum to one truck; the final mark needed 48000 with units N s; errors were including g, signs and units (ER p.3)

parts.ask: Uniform rod AB, length 2a, mass M, held horizontal by vertical strings at C and D (AC = 2a/5, DB = 3a/5); particle P at B: find the largest possible mass of P
parts.ms: M1 moments equation or inequality in X, M, a only (one g may be missing), M0 if T_C appears and never becomes zero; A1 correct, e.g. M(D): Xg·3a/5 = Mg·2a/5; A1 2M/3 (MS p.8)
parts.er: Many did not see that the tension at C is zero at the limit, so made no progress; some assumed equal tensions or used m/M for both masses (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Given the mass of P is M/2, find the tension in the string at C in terms of M and g
parts.ms: M1 moments equation in T_C, M, g, a only (correct number of terms); M0 if T_C = T_D assumed or the (a) value of X used; A1 correct equation, e.g. M(D): T_C·a + ½Mg·3a/5 = Mg·2a/5; A1 Mg/10 (MS p.8)
parts.er: A conventional moments problem, usually done by moments about D; errors were signs and inconsistent g; correct solutions were rare when two simultaneous equations were used (ER p.4)

sources.qp: local:src/WME01/2022-10_01_qp.pdf (examsolutions S3 mirror of Pearson wme01-01-que-20221018.pdf, WME01/01, P72151A, 32 pp.; same document as drive:22_10_QP_M1(1).pdf and papernexus "October 2022 - QP")

sources.er: local:src/WME01/2022-10_01_er.pdf (examsolutions S3 mirror of Pearson wme01-01-pef-20230112.pdf, Principal Examiner Feedback October 2022, WME01_01_ER_2210)

parts.ask: Particle of mass 2 kg held in equilibrium on a rough plane inclined at α (tan α = 3/4) by a horizontal force X N: show that when X = 14.7 there is no friction
parts.ms: M1 equation in F only (resolve along the plane, e.g. 14.7cos α = 2g sin α + F), condone sign errors and sin/cos confusion, M0 if F = 0.5R used; A1 correct equation; A1* conclusion F = 0, or for verification state clearly X = 14.7 ⇒ F = 0 (MS pp.9–10)
parts.er: Show-that: needs reasoned accurate statements and a conclusion; those who assumed F = 0 and derived X = 14.7 often lacked a clear conclusion; using α ≈ 36.9° or 37°, or g = 9.81, was penalised (ER p.4)

parts.ask: μ = 0.5: find the smallest possible value of X
parts.ms: B1 F = 0.5S seen; M1A2 first resolution (e.g. along the plane: X cos α + F = 2g sin α), A2 −1 each error; M1A2 second resolution (e.g. perpendicular: S = X sin α + 2g cos α); A1 4g/11, 3.6 or 3.56/3.57; M0 for both equations if X = 14.7 is used anywhere (MS pp.9–10)
parts.er: Usual approach was resolving parallel and perpendicular then F = 0.5R; the most common error was friction acting down rather than up the plane; also sin/cos confusion, wrong g, non-zero acceleration (ER p.4)

sources.qp: local:src/WME01/2022-10_01_qp.pdf (examsolutions S3 mirror of Pearson wme01-01-que-20221018.pdf, WME01/01, P72151A, 32 pp.; same document as drive:22_10_QP_M1(1).pdf and papernexus "October 2022 - QP")

parts.ask: Lift of mass 250 kg raised by a cable with tension 3616 N; floor exerts 565 N on Alan and 226 N on Bhavana: considering forces on the lift only, find its acceleration
parts.ms: M1 equation of motion for the lift in a only, correct number of terms (3616 − 250g − 565 − 226 = 250a); A1 correct; A1 1.5 (MS p.11)
parts.er: Worst question on the paper: many wrote an equation for the lift but left out the two reaction forces from the children; some got a "correct answer" using the children's weights instead of the forces on the lift (ER pp.3–4)

parts.ask: Find the mass of Alan
parts.ms: M1 equation of motion for Alan only, correct terms (565 − mg = 1.5m); A1ft on their a; A1 50 (MS p.11)
parts.er: Many equated the reaction to the weight (ignoring the acceleration) or to ma (ignoring the weight); a wrong (a) carried forward could still score 2/3 (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Ball projected vertically up at 29.4 m/s from A, 19.6 m above the ground, no rebound: find the distance travelled while its speed is less than 14.7 m/s
parts.ms: M1 complete method for the distance up from speed 14.7 to the top (e.g. 0 = 14.7² − 2gs) and doubling, or distance A-to-top minus distance to the 14.7 point (44.1 − 33.075); A1 correct equation(s); A1 22 or 22.1 (MS p.12)
parts.er: Second worst question: candidates must identify the top section of the flight; good answers used symmetry and doubled; advice: draw a diagram and decide which stage of motion is involved (ER pp.3–4)

parts.ask: Find the time for which the ball moves with speed more than 29.4 m/s
parts.ms: M1 complete method, e.g. 19.6 = 29.4t + ½gt² (the descent from level A); 19.6 = 29.4t − ½gt² and the −19.6 versions are M0 unless the 6 s is subtracted correctly; A1 correct equation(s); A1 0.61 or 0.606; adding/subtracting to 0.606 is M0 (MS p.12)
parts.er: This is the motion from passing A on the way down to the ground; by symmetry, time for 19.6 m starting at 29.4 m/s downwards; alternatives used total time minus time to return to A, or the impact speed (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Sketch the speed-time graph from projection to hitting the ground, showing where it meets the axes
parts.final_form: V-shaped speed-time graph from 29.4, touching t-axis at t = 3
parts.ms: B1 V shape, end speed > 29.4, both arms roughly equally inclined, B0 if a vertical line is drawn at the end; B1 29.4 marked; B1 3 marked (MS p.12)
parts.er: A speed-time (not velocity-time) graph was needed: "v" shape with equal gradients and the second section longer; many drew a straight line as for velocity; a continuous vertical line at the end lost the mark (dotted acceptable) (ER p.5)

sources.qp: local:src/WME01/2022-10_01_qp.pdf (examsolutions S3 mirror of Pearson wme01-01-que-20221018.pdf, WME01/01, P72151A, 32 pp.; same document as drive:22_10_QP_M1(1).pdf and papernexus "October 2022 - QP")

parts.ask: Particle of mass 0.5 kg at rest on a smooth horizontal plane; forces (−3i + 2j) N and (pi + qj) N applied; A moves in the direction of i − 2j: show 2p + q − 4 = 0
parts.ms: M1 add forces, collect i and j; M1 ratio of components equated to 1 : −2 (ratio may be inverted) — writing −3 + p = 1 and 2 + q = −2 without ever using a ratio is M0; A1 correct equation; A1* 2p + q − 4 = 0 (allow 0 = 2p + q − 4 only) (MS p.13)
parts.er: Some equated coefficients to those of i − 2j and solved, gaining nothing more; parallel vectors need components in the same ratio; the printed form must be reached exactly from entirely correct working (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Given p = 5, find the speed of A at t = 4 s
parts.ms: B1 resultant (2i − 4j); M1 F = ma (M0 if g included); M1 v = at with t = 4, u = 0 (M0 if u non-zero); M1 Pythagoras with square root for v, a or F; A1 √1280 = 16√5 = 36 or better (MS p.13)
parts.er: Confusion over whether a vector was a force, acceleration or velocity; initial velocity not always taken as zero; some found the velocity but not the speed (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Particles P and Q, each of mass m, joined by a string over a smooth pulley at the edge of a rough table (μ < 1); Q released from rest; tension is kmg: find k in terms of μ
parts.ms: B1 F = μmg; M1A1 equation of motion for P (mg − kmg = ma); M1A1 equation of motion for Q (kmg − F = ma) — either may be replaced by the whole system mg − F = 2ma; M1 eliminate a to an equation in k and μ only; A1 ½(1 + μ), must appear in (a) (MS pp.14–15)
parts.er: Most wrote equations for P and Q with F = μmg; errors were signs, algebra slips and finding μ in terms of k (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Q starts a distance d from the pulley: find, in terms of d, g and μ, the time for Q to reach the pulley
parts.ms: M1 attempt the acceleration (a = ½g(1 − μ) or equivalent); M1 complete suvat method d = ½at²; A1 correct equation in d, g, t, μ only; A1 any equivalent form (MS pp.14–15)
parts.er: Answers containing k were penalised; few completed a full suvat method after finding the acceleration; unsimplified equivalent answers were credited (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Describe what would happen if μ ≥ 1, giving a reason
parts.ms: B1 P or Q (or the system) would not move, B0 with incorrect extras; DB1 reason, e.g. T = mg ≤ μmg, F = T, a ≤ 0 — forces must be clearly defined; vague "forward force"/"opposite force" is B0 (MS pp.14–15)
parts.er: Many said the system stays at rest, but reasons were often overcomplicated or wrong; needed tension less than or equal to the maximum friction, or an equivalent acceleration statement (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Ship A has velocity (3i + 12j) km/h: find its speed
parts.ms: M1 Pythagoras with square root; A1 √153, 3√17, 12 or better (MS p.16)
parts.er: Almost all correct; a few added 3 + 12 or gave 12.36 (ER p.6)

parts.ask: At noon A is at (−9i + 6j) km, B (velocity pi + qj) at (16i + 6j) km; at time t, AB = (25 − 12t)i − 9tj: find p and q
parts.ms: M1A1A1 position vectors r_A = (−9i + 6j) + t(3i + 12j), r_B = (16i + 6j) + t(pi + qj); M1A1 AB = b − a (allow a − b for M); M1 compare components with the given AB to get an equation in p only and one in q only; A1 both (MS pp.16–17)
parts.er: Errors: multiplying the initial position by t, adding position vectors, dropping the minus in −9j so t did not cancel (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Find the bearing of A from B when the ships are 15 km apart, to the nearest degree
parts.ms: M1A1 |AB|² = 15² giving 225t² − 600t + 400 = 0; A1 t = 4/3 (1.3 or better); DM1 use t to find AB = 9i − 12j (or BA); M1 equation for a relevant angle; A1 37°, 53°, 127° etc.; A1 bearing 323° cao (MS pp.16–17)
parts.er: Some added coefficients ignoring i and j, subtracted (9t)², or forgot to square 15; many did not realise AB was needed for the bearing, used OA and OB, or did not convert to the actual bearing / over-specified the answer (ER p.6)

parts.ask: A train starts from rest at A, accelerates uniformly for T s to 20 m/s, travels at 20 m/s for 3 minutes, then decelerates uniformly to rest at B; the acceleration is twice the deceleration: sketch the speed-time graph
parts.final_form: trapezium with the acceleration steeper than the deceleration; 20 on the speed axis; T, T + 180, 3T + 180 on the time axis
parts.ms: B1 shape with acceleration steeper; B1 20 marked; B1 T, T + 180 and 3T + 180 (or delineators) (MS pp.7-8)
parts.er: Many omitted 3T + 180 from the time axis; common error: halving rather than doubling the deceleration time; symmetric graphs or a steeper deceleration lost the shape mark; many scored only 1/3 for the 20 (ER p.3)

parts.ask: A and B are 4.8 km apart: find T
parts.ms: B1 times T and 2T for acceleration and deceleration; M1 total area = 4800 (must involve a triangle or trapezium; a single suvat for the whole motion is M0), e.g. ½ × 20(180 + 3T + 180) = 4800; A1 at most one error (3 for 180 counts as one); A1 correct; A1 40 (MS pp.7-8)
parts.er: Almost all converted km and minutes; most equated area to distance, a single trapezium with sides 180 and 180 + 3T being most successful; some found a by suvat first (ER pp.3-4)

parts.ask: Find the acceleration during the first T seconds
parts.ms: M1 20 = aT with their T; A1ft 0.5 (MS pp.7-8)
parts.er: Most scored both, with follow-through from (b) (ER p.4)

parts.ask: A (3m kg) and B (m kg) move towards each other, each at 1.5 m/s, and collide directly; afterwards A continues in the same direction and the speeds differ by 1 m/s: find (i) the speed of A and (ii) the speed of B
parts.final_form: A: 0.5 m s⁻¹; B: 1.5 m s⁻¹
parts.ms: B1 speeds v and v + 1 (B faster), set up algebraically before CLM; M1A1 3m(1.5) + m(−1.5) = 3mv + m(v + 1) (M0 if equal speeds after); A1 A 0.5; A1 B 1.5 (MS p.9)
parts.er: Many did not see that B must be faster than A after the collision, so relatively few correct solutions despite using CLM (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Find, in terms of m, the magnitude of the impulse exerted on B
parts.ms: M1A1ft impulse-momentum as a difference of momenta: B: m(1.5 + 1.5) or A: 3m(0.5 − 1.5) (M0 if g included); A1 3m (MS p.9)
parts.er: Better answered, with follow-through; most used B; common error: a wrong sign on one velocity (ER p.4)

parts.ask: P has constant acceleration (−4i + j) m/s² and velocity (14i − 5j) m/s at t = 0: find its speed at t = 2 s
parts.ms: M1 v = (14i − 5j) + 2(−4i + j); M1 Pythagoras; A1 cso √45 (MS p.10)
parts.er: Velocity usually right (a few multiplied the initial velocity by t); a significant number did not go on to find the speed and lost 2/3 (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Find the angle between i and the direction of motion of P at t = 2 s
parts.ms: M1 trig equation for a relevant angle for their v; A1ft e.g. tan⁻¹(3/6); A1 cao, no isw, negative answers A0 (MS p.10)
parts.er: Usually well done with tan; marks lost for adjusting (e.g. 90° + 26.6°) or truncating to 26.5° (ER p.4)

parts.ask: At time T, P moves in the direction of (2i − 3j): find T
parts.ms: M1 v = (14i − 5j) + (−4i + j)T; M1 ratio equation (14 − 4T)/(−5 + T) = 2/(−3) (reciprocal and sign slips allowed for M); A1 correct; A1 3.2; v = k(2i − 3j) solved by calculator allowed if correct (MS pp.10-11)
parts.er: Many equated coefficients with (2i − 3j) or tried a suvat equation instead of using ratios (ER p.4)

parts.ask: A branch AB (1.5 m), modelled as a non-uniform rod of weight W, rests on supports at C and D (AC = 0.24 m, DB = 0.36 m); 150 N upward at B puts it on the point of tilting about C; 225 N downward at B puts it on the point of tilting about D; the centre of mass is x m from C: find (i) W and (ii) x
parts.final_form: W = 300 (N); x = 0.63 (m, from C as defined)
parts.ms: B1 R_D = 0 in scenario 1 or R_C = 0 in scenario 2 (B0 means no other marks); M1A1 scenario 1: M(C): 150 × 1.26 = Wx (M0 if R_D = 0 never used); M1A1 scenario 2: M(D): 225 × 0.36 = W(0.9 − x); dM1 solve simultaneously; A1 W = 300; A1 x = 0.63; g in a moments equation loses that A and both final A marks (MS pp.12-14)
parts.er: Needed one reaction zero in each scenario; wrong reaction set to zero scored nothing; both forces in one equation, too many unknowns, dimensional slips; best: moments about each pivot (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Points P, Q, R on a straight road with PQ = 6x m and QR = 5x m; a vehicle with constant acceleration passes P at u m/s (t = 0) and Q at 2u m/s (t = 12): show x = 3u
parts.ms: M1 equation in u and x for P to Q, e.g. 6x = ½(u + 2u) × 12; A1* (MS p.14)
parts.er: Mostly correct with one or more suvat equations (the report labels this part (b)) (ER p.4)

parts.ask: From Q the acceleration becomes 1.5 m/s² and the vehicle passes R at 3u m/s: find u
parts.ms: M1 equation in u only using x = 3u; A1 (3u)² = (2u)² + 2(1.5)(15u); A1 9 (MS p.14)
parts.er: Errors: initial speed u instead of 2u, t = 12 reused, 2u² for (2u)² (ER pp.4-5)

parts.ask: Find the distance travelled in the first 14 s after passing P
parts.ms: M1A1 distance for the 2 s after Q: 2u(2) + ½(1.5)(2²) = 39; M1 add PQ = 18u; A1 201 (MS p.14)
parts.er: Many used t = 14 in a single suvat equation and scored nothing; some used u instead of 2u for the second stage or 3u as the final speed (ER p.5)

parts.ask: A boat moves at constant speed parallel to the riverbanks, pulled by two horizontal ropes on opposite sides of its line of motion (500 N at 40°, P N at α°) against a 900 N resistance: find (i) α and (ii) P
parts.final_form: α = 32 or better (31.87); P = 610 or better (608.7)
parts.ms: M1A1 perpendicular: 500 sin 40° = P sin α; M1A1 parallel: 500 cos 40° + P cos α = 900 (a = 0 if F = ma used); M1A1 tan α = 500 sin 40°/(900 − 500 cos 40°), α = 32; M1A1 P = 610; ALT triangle of forces with cosine/sine rule or Lami; over-accuracy penalised once (MS pp.15-16)
parts.er: Occasionally an ma term despite constant velocity; 900 N wrongly included perpendicular; dividing to get tan α worked well; early rounding gave inaccurate answers (ER p.5)

parts.ask: A lift of mass m carries box Q on its floor with box P on Q; cable tension 42mg/5; everything accelerates upwards at 2g/5: find the combined mass of P and Q in terms of m
parts.ms: M1 equation of motion for the whole system with the correct total mass: 42mg/5 − (m + M)g = (m + M)(2g/5); A1 correct; dM1 rearrange to a multiple of m; A1 5m (MS p.17)
parts.er: By far the most challenging question (many zeros); main error: using m (the lift alone) in the ma term for the whole system (ER pp.3, 5)

parts.ask: The force on P from Q is 14mg/5: find the mass of P in terms of m
parts.ms: M1 equation of motion for P alone: 14mg/5 − pg = p(2g/5); A1 correct; A1 2m (or find Q and subtract from 5m) (MS pp.17-18)
parts.er: Fewer attempts; main error: including the cable tension in the forces on P; many still scored full marks after failing (a) (ER p.5)

parts.ask: A 2 kg parcel is pulled up a rough plane inclined at 30° (μ = 0.3) by an 18 N force at 40° to the plane, in the vertical plane of a line of greatest slope: find its acceleration
parts.ms: M1A1 R + 18 sin 40° = 2g cos 30°; M1A1A1 18 cos 40° − F − 2g sin 30° = 2a (A1 at most one error); B1 F = 0.3R; dM1 eliminate F and R; A1 1.18 or 1.2 (MS pp.18-19)
parts.er: Many full marks, but some skipped it or scored only the B1; common error: R = 2g cos 30° (ignoring the force component); sin/cos confusion; over-specified a (ER p.5)

parts.ask: P passes A at 2 m/s moving up the line of greatest slope towards B, AB = 5 m: find its speed at B
parts.ms: M1A1ft v² = 2² + 2a(5) with their a; A1 cao (a = 1.2 gives 4) (MS pp.18-19)
parts.er: Final mark often lost through premature rounding of a (ER p.5)

parts.ask: The 18 N force is removed at B and P comes to rest at C: determine whether P remains at rest at C, showing all stages
parts.final_form: conclusion: P will not remain at rest (2g sin 30° > 0.3 × 2g cos 30°), from a comparison
parts.ms: B1 new R = 2g cos 30° (= g√3); M1 maximum friction 0.3 × 2g cos 30° (M0 if the old R is used); dM1 compare with the weight component 2g sin 30° (or find the net force or acceleration); A1 correct conclusion from fully correct working (MS pp.18-19)
parts.er: Good discriminator; some reused R from (a) and scored nothing; needed a comparison of maximum friction with the weight component and a conclusion; adding the two forces lost both marks (ER p.5)

parts.ask: A (4 kg, speed 2u) and B (2 kg, speed 3u) move towards each other and collide directly; B rebounds with speed 2u: find the speed of A afterwards in terms of u
parts.ms: M1 CLM (or equate impulses), consistent extra g allowed; A1 4(2u) − 2(3u) = 4v + 2(2u); A1 ½u, must be positive (MS p.7)
parts.er: Mostly correct by CLM; equating impulses caused more sign errors; many gave a negative speed and lost the final mark (ER p.3)

parts.ask: State the direction of motion of A after the collision
parts.ms: B1 reversed or opposite direction; "changed", "to the left", "backwards", "away from B" not accepted; depends on ±½u in (a) (MS p.7)
parts.er: Imprecise answers ("to the left", "west", "changed") lost the mark (ER p.3)

parts.ask: Find the magnitude of the impulse received by B, stating the units
parts.final_form: 10u N s (or kg m s⁻¹), positive, units required
parts.ms: M1 impulse-momentum for B, 2(2u + 3u), or for A (M0 if g included); A1 correct; A1 10u N s with units (MS p.7)
parts.er: B was the sensible choice (both velocities given); a significant minority gave a negative magnitude; units often omitted or wrong (ER p.3)

parts.ask: Particle P in equilibrium on a smooth horizontal plane under F1 = (3ci + 4cj), F2 = (−14i + 7j) and F3 N: find F3 in terms of c, i and j
parts.final_form: F3 = (14 − 3c)i + (−7 − 4c)j (i, j form, not a column vector)
parts.ms: M1 F1 + F2 + F3 = 0 (F3 = F1 + F2 is M0); A1 cao, isw (MS pp.8-9)
parts.er: Mostly correct; a small proportion used F3 = F1 + F2 (ER p.4)

parts.ask: F3 is removed and c = 2: find the angle between i and the resultant force
parts.final_form: angle with i ≈ 118.1°: the scheme accepts 120° or better (118.07…) or the reflex 240° or better (241.93…); in radians 2.1 or better (2.06…) or 4.2 or better (4.22…)
parts.ms: M1 resultant F1 + F2 = −8i + 15j (or −F3); M1 trig for a relevant angle; A1ft any relevant angle (e.g. tan⁻¹(15/8)); A1 cso 120 or better (118.07…) or 240 or better (241.93…) (MS pp.8-9)
parts.er: Many stopped at 28° or 62° instead of the angle with i; a few gave a bearing or compass direction (ER p.4)

parts.ask: P has mass m kg and its acceleration has magnitude 8.5 m/s²: find m
parts.ms: M1 Pythagoras on the resultant (17) or on a; M1 |R| = 8.5m; A1ft 17 = 8.5m; A1 cso 2 (MS pp.8-9)
parts.er: Generally well answered; most scored at least 3/4 thanks to the follow-through (ER p.4)

parts.ask: A 0.2 kg book falls from rest from a shelf 1.5 m above the floor; student A models it as a particle falling freely: find the time to reach the floor
parts.ms: M1 1.5 = ½gt² (a = g); A1 correct; A1 0.55 or 0.553 (MS p.10)
parts.er: All or nothing; exact-form answers lost the A mark; a negative t² should have signalled a sign error (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Student B models a constant resistance R N; the book takes 0.6 s: find R
parts.ms: M1A1 1.5 = ½a(0.6)² (a ≠ g); M1A1 0.2g − R = 0.2a; A1 0.293 or 0.29; g = 9.81 and fraction answers penalised once per question (MS p.10)
parts.er: Less successful: the weight often missing from the equation of motion, a few used g as the acceleration; marks lost for not giving 2 or 3 s.f. or for fractions (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Uniform beam AB (m kg, 2 m) hangs horizontally from ropes at C (AC = 0.6 m) and D (DB = 0.2 m); a particle of mass pm kg is attached at A and the tension at C is four times that at D: find the exact value of p
parts.ms: B1 T and 4T placed correctly; M1A1 vertical: 5T = pmg + mg (or a moments equation); M1A1 e.g. M(A): 4T(0.6) + T(1.8) = mg(1); M1 eliminate T to an equation in p; A1 4/21 exact (MS pp.11-12)
parts.er: Usually vertical resolution then moments (or two moments equations); missing g, sign and length errors, algebra too complicated to finish; a few did not give an exact answer (ER p.4)

parts.ask: The particle at A is replaced by one of mass qm kg and the beam is on the point of tilting: find the exact value of q
parts.ms: B1 tension at D is zero; M1A1 M(C): qmg(0.6) = mg(0.4) (M0 if T_D never zero); A1 2/3 (MS pp.11-12)
parts.er: Sometimes omitted; most saw T_D = 0 and took moments about C; two-equation methods less successful; some rounded to 0.67 (ER p.4)

parts.ask: State how the modelling assumption that the beam is uniform has been used
parts.final_form: one statement: the weight (centre of mass) of the beam acts at its midpoint
parts.ms: B1 centre of mass/weight at the middle; incorrect extras penalised (MS p.11)
parts.er: Reasonably well answered; wrong: "remains straight", "does not bend", "equal tensions", "weight acts at a single point" without saying the centre (ER p.4)

parts.ask: A car starts from rest, accelerates uniformly for 30 s to V m/s, then constant speed until t = T: show the distance by time T is V(T − 15) m
parts.ms: M1 area (trapezium, triangle + rectangle) or suvat; A1* (MS pp.13-14)
parts.er: Usually fine; some wrote the given answer after incorrect working (ER p.4)

parts.ask: A motorbike starts from rest at t = 10, accelerates uniformly for 40 s with the same acceleration as the car, travels at constant speed for 10 s, then decelerates uniformly to V at time T: sketch its speed-time graph on Figure 2
parts.final_form: acceleration line parallel to the car's, flat section, then down to meet the car's graph at (T, V); 10, 50, 60 marked
parts.ms: B1 shape with parallel acceleration lines meeting at (T, V), no continuous vertical line at T; B1 10, 50, 60 marked (independent); B0B0 if not drawn on the given figure (MS pp.13-14)
parts.er: Shape usually fine; most common error: 40 and 50 marked instead of 50 and 60, which spoiled (d) (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Show that the constant speed of the motorbike is 4V/3 m/s
parts.ms: M1 equal gradients: speed/40 = V/30; A1* (MS pp.13-14)
parts.er: Many did not use the equal accelerations; some skipped (c) but used its result in (d); some fudged solutions (ER p.4)

parts.ask: At time T both have travelled the same distance: find T
parts.ms: M1A1A1 motorbike's total area in V and T: ½(4V/3)(40) + (4V/3)(10) + ½(4V/3 + V)(T − 60); M1 equate to V(T − 15) (independent); A1 90; ALT equate the trapezium and parallelogram areas between the graphs (MS pp.13-14)
parts.er: Well answered if (b) was right; common errors: (4V/3 − V) instead of (4V/3 + V) for the last trapezium, treating it as a triangle, wrong times (50 for 60, 40 for 50) (ER pp.4-5)

parts.ask: A particle of weight W N at rest on a rough horizontal surface (μ = 1/4) is pushed by a force P N directed downwards at α to the horizontal (tan α = 4/3); the particle does not move: show P ≤ 5W/8
parts.final_form: printed inequality P ≤ 5W/8 from correct use of F ≤ μR
parts.ms: M1A1 vertical: R − P sin α = W (M0 for an inequality); M1A1 horizontal: F = P cos α; M1 F ≤ ¼R (M0 for < or >); M1 eliminate F and R to an inequality/equation in P and W; A1* cso with the inequality used correctly (MS p.15)
parts.er: W treated as a mass (Wg); sign error taking P's component upwards; many used the limiting equation throughout and could not earn the final mark by just writing ≤ on the last line (ER p.5)

parts.ask: A car (1200 kg) tows a trailer (600 kg) up a road with sin α = 1/12; driving force 3000 N, acceleration 0.75 m/s², resistances 2R (car) and R (trailer); tow bar a light rod: show R = 60
parts.ms: M1 whole system (or both bodies with T eliminated): 3000 − 1800g sin α − 3R = 1800(0.75); A1 at most one error; A1 correct; A1* with an intermediate line (MS p.16)
parts.er: Most challenging question (many zeros); whole-system equation best; separate equations confused terms; some treated it as equilibrium, did not resolve weights, or added friction (ER pp.3, 5)

parts.ask: Find the tension in the tow bar
parts.ms: M1A1 trailer: T − 600g sin α − 60 = 600(0.75) (or the car); A1 1000 (MS p.16)
parts.er: Some forgot the ma term; wrong combinations of terms for car/trailer showed weak understanding of connected bodies (ER pp.5-6)

parts.ask: The tow bar breaks at 12 m/s; the trailer's resistance is unchanged: find the further distance it moves before first coming to rest
parts.ms: M1A1 −60 − 600g sin α = 600a (a = −11/12); M1 0 = 12² + 2ad with a calculated a ≠ g; A1 78.5 or 79 (MS p.16)
parts.er: Many kept a = 0.75; some omitted R or had it acting up the slope; answer to 2 or 3 s.f. required (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Robot R moves with constant velocity across a 50 m square floor (centre O, i along AB, j along AD); at t = 0 it is at (−2i + j) m and at t = 11 at (9i + 23j) m: find r in terms of t, i and j
parts.ms: M1 velocity = displacement/11; M1 r with correct structure; A1 cao; column-vector answers penalised once (MS p.17)
parts.er: Generally understood; column-vector answers lost the final mark (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Robot S leaves corner C at t = 0 with velocity (−i − j) m/s: write down s
parts.ms: B1 any correct form (MS p.17)
parts.er: Common error: measuring from corner A, giving (50 − t)i + (50 − t)j; some wrote −ti − tj (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Show that SR = [(2t − 27)i + (3t − 24)j] m
parts.ms: M1 r − s (or s − r) with their r and s; A1* (MS p.17)
parts.er: Mostly subtraction of position vectors; the given answer exposed errors in (b); the last line must match the printed answer (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Find the time when the distance between R and S is a minimum
parts.ms: M1 |SR| or |SR|² by Pythagoras; A1 13t² − 252t + 1305; A1 9.7 or better (differentiation, completing the square or calculator) (MS p.17)
parts.er: Some stopped at the distance expression or set it to zero; most expanded and differentiated or completed the square; only t was required (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Uniform beam AB (weight 24 N, length 6 m) hangs horizontally from vertical ropes at C and D (AC = x m, CD = 2 m); tension at C is double that at D: find (i) the tension at D and (ii) x
parts.ms: M1A1 moments equation in x and T, e.g. M(A): 2T·x + T(x + 2) = 24 × 3 (M0 if no x); M1 second equation (vertical 3T = 24, or another moments equation); A1 T = 8; A1 x = 7/3; T and 2T swapped, or 24g used, max M1A0M1A0A0 (MS p.7)
parts.er: Best-answered question; best route: resolve vertically for T then take moments; two moments equations took longer and caused manipulation errors; errors: T and 2T confused, 24g for 24, not using T_C = 2T_D, wrong lengths, bracket sign errors; using the diagram would have helped (ER p.3)

parts.ask: Acceleration-time graph of a car from A to B: −0.5 m/s² for 0-4 s, 0 for 4-10 s, 1.2 m/s² for 10-20 s; speed 8 m/s at A (t = 0) and v at B (t = 20): show v = 18
parts.ms: M1 speed at t = 4: w = 8 − 0.5 × 4 = 6 (M0 if u = 0); M1 v = w + 1.2 × 10 starting from w; A1* (MS p.8)
parts.er: Needed v = 6 at t = 4, still 6 at t = 10, then 18; a single suvat over the whole motion (e.g. v = 8 + 0.5 × 20) scored nothing; show-that needs full working (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Sketch a speed-time graph from A to B
parts.final_form: three connected lines: 8 down to 6 (0-4), level 6 (4-10), up to 18 (10-20); labels 4, 10, 20 and 6, 8, 18
parts.ms: B1 shape (solid vertical lines B0); B1 time labels 4, 10, 20; B1 speed labels 6, 8, 18 (MS p.8)
parts.er: Needed three connected straight lines (negative, zero, positive gradient); intermediate solid vertical lines penalised; some drew the middle phase along the t-axis; curves and wrong shapes seen (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Find the distance AB
parts.ms: M1 area under their three-section graph (or suvat per section: 28 + 36 + 120); A1ft at most one error; A1ft correct, e.g. ½(8 + 6)4 + 6 × 6 + ½(6 + 18)10; A1 184 (MS p.8)
parts.er: Two trapezia and a rectangle, or suvat per phase; a correct (b) graph usually meant success; a single suvat for the whole motion scored nothing (ER p.4)

parts.ask: A hammer (1.8 kg) moving down at 10 m/s hits a stationary tent peg (0.2 kg); modelled as particles in a direct collision, they move on together at v m/s: find v
parts.er: Mostly correct by CLM; sign errors or wrong mass/velocity pairings (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Find the magnitude of the impulse on the tent peg from the hammer, stating the units
parts.final_form: 1.8 N s (or kg m s⁻¹), units required
parts.ms: M1A1 impulse-momentum for the peg 0.2(v − 0) or hammer −I = 1.8(v − 10) (M0 if g included); A1 1.8 N s with units (MS p.9)
parts.er: Units often omitted or wrong; including g gave a dimensionally wrong expression and no marks (ER p.4)

parts.ask: The ground exerts a constant resistance R N and they stop after 12 cm: find R
parts.ms: M1A1 0 = 9² + 2a(0.12) (a = −337.5); M1A1 2g − R = 2a with consistent signs; A1 690 or 695; u = 10 instead of 9 max 2/5; s = 12 max 3/5; ALTs via time and impulse, or work-energy (MS pp.9-10)
parts.er: Many used 12 m instead of 0.12 m; inconsistent signs in the equation of motion; omitting the weight was a more serious error; many failed to round to 2 or 3 s.f. after g = 9.8 (ER p.4)

parts.ask: P has constant acceleration (−λi + 2λj) m/s² (λ > 0) and velocity (5i − 8j) m/s at t = 0: find its velocity at t = 5 in terms of i, j and λ
parts.final_form: (5i − 8j) + 5(−λi + 2λj) m s⁻¹, isw (not a column vector for A1)
parts.ms: M1 v = u + at in vector form; A1 correct with t = 5 (MS p.11)
parts.er: Mostly correct; some confused v and a or misused v = u + at, often without quoting a formula (ER p.4)

parts.ask: The speed at t = 5 is 13 m/s: show that 25λ² − 42λ − 16 = 0
parts.ms: M1 collect components and Pythagoras: 13 = √((5 − 5λ)² + (−8 + 10λ)²); A1 correct; A1* cso with brackets expanded (MS p.11)
parts.er: Mostly fine; a minority jumped from the unsimplified equation to the given answer or did not reach exactly the printed form; show-that needs every step (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Find the direction of motion of P at t = 4, as a bearing to the nearest degree
parts.ms: B1 acceleration −2i + 4j (λ = 2); M1A1 velocity at t = 4: (5i − 8j) + 4(−2i + 4j) = −3i + 8j; M1 trig for a relevant angle with their velocity; A1 339; working with both λ values loses only the last mark (MS p.11)
parts.er: λ = 2 commonly used, but some used t = 5; a few used a displacement vector; many could not get the three-figure bearing or did not round to the nearest degree (ER p.5)

parts.ask: A small 0.2 kg ring on a fixed rough vertical rod is attached to a taut string at θ to the rod (tan θ = 12/5, string pulling upwards and outwards); the ring is in equilibrium with tension 10 N: find the magnitude of the friction
parts.ms: M1A1 resolve vertically: F = 10cos θ − 0.2g (or reverse); A1 1.9 or 1.89 (MS p.12)
parts.er: Most challenging question (a quarter scored zero); no clear force diagram, R and F confused, R drawn vertical; some used F = μR although not in limiting equilibrium (ER pp.3, 5)

parts.ask: State the direction of the frictional force on the ring
parts.ms: A1 down, from a correct (possibly unrounded) answer to (a); anything else A0 (MS p.12)
parts.er: Many with a correct value gave the wrong direction (ER p.5)

parts.ask: μ = 1/4 and the tension T can vary with the ring in equilibrium: find (i) the minimum and (ii) the maximum value of T
parts.final_form: min T = 3.2 or 3.19 N (0.325g); max T = 13 or 12.7 N (1.3g); labelled
parts.ms: M1A1 R = T sin θ = 12T/13 (M0 if T = 10); B1 F = ¼R; M1 resolve parallel to the rod (M0 with T = 10 or F from (a)); A1 min: T cos θ = 0.2g − F; A1 max: T cos θ = 0.2g + F; A1 3.2 or 3.19; A1 13 or 12.7; wrongly labelled answers lose the last two marks; over-accuracy penalised once (MS p.12)
parts.er: Reasonable attempts but unclear which case gives the maximum and which the minimum; over-specified answers after g = 9.8 lost marks (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Ship P leaves (15i + 36j) km at 12:00 and is at (20i + 34j) km at 12:30, with constant velocity: show its velocity is (10i − 4j) km/h
parts.ms: M1 difference of positions over 0.5 h (30 min allowed for M; missing brackets M1A0); A1* (MS pp.13-14)
parts.er: Mostly correct; t = 30 could earn the M mark; column-vector answers penalised (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Find p, the position of P t hours after 12:00, in terms of i, j and t
parts.ms: M1 correct structure; A1 in terms of i, j and t (MS pp.13-14)
parts.er: Done well (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Ship Q has q = (42 − 8t)i + (9 + 14t)j: (i) verify that P and Q would collide at 13:30 and (ii) find the position vector of the collision point
parts.final_form: both p and q equal 30i + 30j at t = 1.5
parts.ms: (i) M1 substitute t = 1.5 into both (or equate components, or use a ratio and verify); A1 p = 30i + 30j; A1 q = 30i + 30j; (ii) B1 30i + 30j (MS pp.13-14)
parts.er: Many verified only one component, so the verification was incomplete; the collision position was usually correct (ER p.6)

parts.ask: At 12:30 Q turns due north at 15 km/h; P keeps its velocity: find the exact distance between P and Q at 14:30
parts.ms: B1 P at 14:30: 40i + 26j; M1 Q at 12:30 from t = 0.5 (38i + 16j); B1 new velocity 15j; M1 Q at 14:30 = (38i + 16j) + 2(15j) (M0 if 2.5 used); A1 38i + 46j; dM1 Pythagoras; A1 2√101 (MS pp.13-14)
parts.er: Mixed success; writing 15 km/h north as 15j was a stumbling block (scalars mixed with vectors); keeping everything in t led to inconsistent times; substituting t = 2.5 in both p and q ignored the change of course and scored at most 1/7 (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Block A (m) on a rough plane (μ = 1/3, tan α = 7/24) joined over a small smooth pulley at the top to B (km) hanging; released, A moves up the plane with tension 4mg/3: find the magnitude of A's acceleration in terms of g
parts.final_form: a = 11g/15 (0.73g or better), a multiple of g
parts.ms: Printed (9) covers (a)(i) and (ii); the scheme marks (i) 6 and (ii) 3. M1A1 for A: 4mg/3 − mg sin α − F = ma; M1A1 R = mg cos α; M1 F = ⅓R in an equation; A1 11g/15 (MS p.15)
parts.er: Familiar set-up; common error: omitting a force (omitting the weight component still allowed R and F = μR marks; omitting friction usually lost them); some did not give a as a multiple of g (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Find the value of k
parts.ms: M1 for B: kmg − 4mg/3 = kma (km on both sides; whole-system equation kmg − mg sin α − F = (k + 1)ma allowed); A1 correct; A1 5 (MS p.15)
parts.er: Less successful: k omitted from kma or kmg; whole-system attempts without the combined mass; slips in solving or a wrong a carried forward (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Find the magnitude of the resultant force exerted on the pulley by the string, in terms of m and g
parts.ms: M1A1 2T cos((90° − α)/2), or cosine rule with angle 90° + α, or components (T cos α)² + (T + T sin α)²; dM1 substitute T = 4mg/3 and trig; A1 32mg/15 (MS pp.15-16)
parts.er: Often omitted or no valid attempt; some combined ma terms instead of tension components; best: 2T cos((90° − α)/2); cosine-rule users often used 90° − α instead of 90° + α (wrong triangle) (ER p.6)

parts.ask: A small smooth ring on a light string fixed at A and B on a ceiling rests at C vertically below B, held by a horizontal 2 N force; the string makes θ with the ceiling at A (tan θ = 3/4): find the tension T
parts.ms: M1 horizontal equilibrium 2 = T cos θ (sin/cos confusion condoned); A1 correct; A1 2.5; different tensions in the two parts of the string can score (a) only (MS p.7)
parts.er: Mostly resolved horizontally to T cos θ = 2 correctly; a few treated the static ring as accelerating (ER pp.3-4)

parts.ask: Find the mass M of the ring
parts.ms: M1 vertical equilibrium T + T sin θ = Mg (same tension in both parts; missing g condoned for M); A1 correct; A1 0.41 or 0.408 (MS p.7)
parts.er: A significant number omitted one of the vertical forces and lost all 3 marks; answers left as 0.4, 4/g or 20/49 lost the final mark; g = 9.81 or 10, omitted g, different tensions in the two parts (ER pp.3-4)

parts.ask: A (5 kg, 3 m/s) and B (x kg, x m/s) move towards each other and collide directly; afterwards A moves at 1 m/s in the same direction and B at 1.5 m/s: find x
parts.ms: M1 CLM (or equate impulses) to an equation in x only, sign errors and extra g condoned; A1 5(3) − x² = 5(1) + 1.5x; A1 2.5, rejecting −4 if seen (MS p.8)
parts.er: Generally well done but poor algebra on the quadratic (x times x becoming 2x); sign error on 1.5; rejecting −4 by bracketing it is unclear; some took x = 2.5 as the mass and −4 as the velocity (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Find the magnitude of the impulse exerted on A by B
parts.final_form: 10 N s (positive; A0 if another answer is also given)
parts.ms: M1 impulse-momentum for A or B as a difference of momenta (M0 if g included or momenta added without a formula); A1 5(1 − 3) or 2.5(1.5 + 2.5); A1 10 (MS p.8)
parts.er: Using A was best; marks lost for leaving a negative answer instead of the magnitude; using B relied on a possibly wrong x (ER p.4)
