parts.ask: A van with constant acceleration passes A at u m/s and B 20 s later at 28 m/s; AB = 400 m: show u = 12
parts.ms: M1 complete method, e.g. 400 = ½(u + 28) × 20 (two equations with a eliminated also fine); A1* cso; using u = 12 to find a and then "showing" u = 12 scores nothing (MS pp.9-10)
parts.er: Usually s = ½(u + v)t; some used long multi-equation routes; a few quoted wrong formulae such as s = ½(u − v)t (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Find the time for the van to travel from A to the midpoint of AB
parts.final_form: t = 5√29 − 15 ≈ 11.9 s (12 or better; reject the negative root)
parts.ms: M1A1 acceleration from a suvat equation with u = 12 (a = 0.8); M1A1 200 = 12t + 0.4t² (or find v = √464 first) using their a and 12; A1 12 or better (MS pp.9-10)
parts.er: Most found a and solved a quadratic; common errors: s = 200 with u = 12 and v = 28, or assuming half the time or half the speed at half the distance (ER p.4)

parts.ask: The van (1200 kg) has constant resistance 260 N: find the driving force
parts.ms: M1 F = ma with the correct terms (M0 if a = g): D − 260 = 1200(0.8); A1ft; A1 1220 (MS pp.9-10)
parts.er: Worst-answered part of Q3: many wrote 1200(0.8) − 260 = 700, usually without a complete equation of motion (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Horizontal forces P (X N) and Q (5√3 N) act on a particle with 150° between their directions; the resultant has magnitude √129 N: find X
parts.ms: Printed (8) covers (i) and (ii); the scheme marks them 4 + 4. M1A1 equation in X only via the correct vector triangle (angle 30°): 129 = X² + 75 − 2X(5√3)cos 30°, or components; M1 solve; A1 18; using 150° in the sine or cosine rule (wrong triangle) earns no M marks (MS pp.11-13)
parts.er: Most challenging question by far; errors: assuming equilibrium (X cos 30° = 5√3), the wrong triangle with 150° opposite the resultant, adding components and equating to √129; the most successful used components or a vector triangle with the cosine rule (ER pp.3, 5)

parts.ask: Find the angle between Q and the resultant, to the nearest degree
parts.ms: M2A1A1 equation in the angle using X (sine rule 18/sin θ = √129/sin 30°, cosine rule or scalar product); or M1A1 a relevant angle (22.4°, 37.6° or 52.4°) then M1A1 128° (MS pp.12-13)
parts.er: Those who found the obtuse angle had mostly sketched a correct diagram; many stopped at 52° or 38° for 2 marks; some did not round to the nearest degree (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Uniform beam AB (30 kg, 3 m) on supports C and D (AC = DB = 0.4 m); a 55 kg person stands at P, CP = x (0 < x < 2.2): show that the reaction at C is (686 − 245x) N
parts.final_form: printed (686 − 245x) N, with at least one intermediate line
parts.ms: M1A1 M(D): 2.2R_C = 55g(2.2 − x) + 30g(1.1) (or two equations eliminating R_D; not via R_C = 4R_D); A1* (MS pp.14-15)
parts.er: Moments about D was usual and many scored 3; other points with elimination gave more work and errors (ER p.5)

parts.ask: The reaction at C is four times the reaction at D: find x
parts.ms: M1 R_C = 4R_D; M1A1 equation in x only, e.g. (5/4)(686 − 245x) = 85g using (a); A1 0.08 (MS pp.14-15)
parts.er: Simplest was vertical resolution with (a); a fairly common mistake was using the 4:1 relation the wrong way round (ER p.5)

parts.ask: The person steps off and a package of mass M kg is placed at A; the beam is on the point of tilting about C: find M
parts.ms: M1 reaction at D = 0 (M0 otherwise) with an equation in M only: M(C): 0.4Mg = 1.1(30g); A1 correct; A1 82.5 or 83 (MS pp.14-15)
parts.er: No credit without realising the reaction at D is zero; common error: keeping the 55 kg term after the person stepped off; some reused the (a) expression for R_C (ER p.5)

parts.ask: A particle is projected vertically up at 24 m/s from A, 2.5 m above ground point B, and lands at B with speed V: find V
parts.ms: M1 equation in V only (V² = 24² + 2g(2.5), or via the top); A1 correct with consistent signs; A1 25 (MS pp.16-17)
parts.er: One suvat for the whole motion or two stages via the top; errors: signs, wrong formulae, using 24 m/s at the top or zero speed at A (ER pp.5-6)

parts.ask: Find the time taken to reach B
parts.ms: M1A1 equation in t only, e.g. 25 = −24 + gt or 2.5 = −24t + ½gt²; A1 5 (MS pp.16-17)
parts.er: One-, two- or three-step methods seen; the M mark needed a complete method; sign errors common (ER p.6)

parts.ask: C is 10 m above A: find the length of time for which the particle is above C
parts.ms: M1A1 10 = 24t − ½gt² (or speed at C from W² = 24² − 20g); M1 complete method, e.g. difference of the roots (a range t1 < t < t2 accepted); A1 4, 4.0 or 3.98 (MS pp.16-17)
parts.er: Best method: solve 10 = 24t − ½gt² and take the difference of the roots; errors: signs, taking 10 m from B or 10 m below the top (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Sketch a speed-time graph from projection to reaching B (no further calculation)
parts.final_form: V shape, vertex on the t-axis, equal-magnitude gradients, end higher than start; 24, 25 and 5 labelled
parts.ms: B1 shape; B1ft labels 24, 25, 5; neither mark for a velocity-time graph (MS pp.16-17)
parts.er: Needed a symmetrical V with the second part longer and labels 24, V and the time; candidates must distinguish speed-time from velocity-time graphs (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Ship S at (19i + 22j) km at midnight moves with velocity (12i − 16j) km/h: find its speed
parts.ms: M1 Pythagoras; A1 20 (MS pp.18-19)
parts.er: Virtually all correct (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Find s, its position t hours after midnight, in terms of i, j and t
parts.final_form: s = (19i + 22j) + t(12i − 16j), in i, j form (not a column vector)
parts.ms: M1 correct structure; A1 correct with i and j (MS pp.18-19)
parts.er: Mostly correct; column-vector-only answers were penalised but rare (ER p.6)

parts.ask: A lighthouse is at (26i + 15j) km and ships must stay more than 1.3 km away: (i) find t when S is closest to it; (ii) hence decide whether S can safely continue
parts.final_form: (i) t = 0.49; (ii) closest distance 1.4 km > 1.3 so safe
parts.ms: (i) M1A1 LS = (12t − 7)i + (7 − 16t)j; M1A1 |LS|² = 400t² − 392t + 98; A1 t = 0.49 (calculator, completing the square, differentiation or LS · v = 0 accepted); (ii) M1 √1.96 = 1.4; A1cso compare 1.4 with 1.3 and conclude safe (MS pp.18-19)
parts.er: Much harder: Pythagoras on the position of S or L instead of SL; equating components or ratios from past papers was irrelevant; equating the quadratic to 1.3²; comparing d² rather than d with 1.3; some concluded unsafe despite 1.4 km (ER p.6)

parts.ask: P (m) on a rough plane (tan α = 5/12) joined over a smooth pulley at the top to Q (0.5m) hanging; limiting equilibrium with P about to slip up the plane: find μ
parts.ms: M1A1 R = mg cos α; M1A1 P: T = mg sin α + F (if F = ma used, a must be 0); B1 T = 0.5mg; B1 F = μR; dM1 0.5mg = 5mg/13 + μ(12mg/13); A1 1/8 (MS p.20)
parts.er: Most found R and used F = μR; weaker answers added a spurious ma term instead of limiting equilibrium; sign, sin/cos and algebra errors (ER p.7)

parts.ask: The string breaks and P slides down the plane: find its speed V after 0.8 m
parts.ms: M1A1 mg sin α − F = ma (a = 7g/26); M1 V² = 2a(0.8) with their a (M0 with g); A1 2.1 or 2.05 (MS p.20)
parts.er: Few fully correct: friction in the wrong direction; 2.06 from premature rounding of a to 2.64 (ER p.7)

parts.ask: A (m) and B (3m) joined by a slack light inextensible string on a smooth plane; A is projected away from B with speed U; after the string becomes taut they share speed S: find S in terms of U
parts.ms: M1 CLM mU = mS + 3mS, or two impulse-momentum equations with I eliminated; A1 U/4 cao (A0 if m not cancelled) (MS p.7)

parts.ask: Find, in terms of m and U, the magnitude of the impulse exerted on A when the string becomes taut
parts.ms: M1 impulse-momentum for A, m(U − U/4), or for B, 3m(U/4) (M0 if m omitted or g included); A1ft on their S; A1 3mU/4 (MS p.7)

parts.ask: Forces P (10 N due west) and Q (8 N on a bearing of 330°) act on a particle; F = P + Q: find the magnitude of F
parts.ms: M1 correct vector triangle with lengths and angle (or two correct component sums); M1 cosine rule (any angle < 180°) or Pythagoras on combined components; A1 F² = 8² + 10² − 2·8·10 cos 120°; A1 √244, 2√61 or 16 or better; a scale drawing scores max M1 (MS p.8)

parts.ask: P (4m) hangs below Q (2m) on a light string; a second string attached to Q pulls up; both accelerate downwards and the connecting tension is 3mg: find the tension in the upper string
parts.ms: M1A1 M1A1 any two of: P: 4mg − 3mg = 4ma; whole: 6mg − T = 6ma; Q: 2mg + 3mg − T = 2ma (the mass in the ma term identifies the body); DM1 solve for T in terms of mg; A1 4.5mg (MS p.9)

parts.ask: Non-uniform rod AB (6.5 m, 1.2 kg, centre of mass 3 m from A) rests on a step, overhanging the edge C by 1.5 m; 4 kg particle at B and M kg at D (AD = 0.5 m); rod stays horizontal: find the smallest M
parts.ms: M1 equation in M only (moments about C with tilting about C), missing g condoned; A1 M(C): 4.5Mg + 2(1.2g) = 1.5(4g); A1 0.8 (MS p.10)

parts.ask: The particles are removed and a new particle is placed at E (EB = 0.9 m); the rod is on the point of tilting about C: find the magnitude of the force on the rod at C
parts.ms: M1 equation in R_C only, e.g. M(E): 0.6R_C = 2.6(1.2g), or eliminate the particle's weight (X = 4); A1 correct; A1 5.2g, 51 or 51.0, isw (MS p.10)

parts.ask: A parachute and box (modelled as a 250 kg particle) dropped from rest at 520 m fall freely for 5 s: find the distance fallen in the first 5 s
After 5 s the parachute opens and gives a 3200 N resistance: find the landing speed
parts.ms: B1 speed at 5 s = 49; M1A1 N2L 250g − 3200 = 250a; A1 a = −3 (deceleration 3); M1A1ft v² = 49² − 2(3)(520 − 122.5) (M0 if u = 0 or s = 520); A1 4 (MS pp.11-12)

parts.ask: Find the total time from release to landing
parts.ms: M1 time after opening with the new a, e.g. 4 = 49 − 3t (M0 for s = 520 or u = 0); A1 t = 15 (the other quadratic root 53/3 gives v < 0); A1ft total 20 (MS pp.11-12)

parts.ask: Sketch a speed-time graph from release to landing
parts.final_form: two straight lines: rising from the origin to 49 at t = 5, then falling to 4 (not to zero) at t = 20
parts.ms: B1 shape (B0 for a continuous vertical line at the end or ending on the t-axis); B1ft 49, 4, 5 and 20 shown; B0ft if it assumes it stops on reaching the ground (MS pp.11-12)

parts.ask: A box of mass m is pulled at constant speed along a rough horizontal plane (μ = 1/3) by a rope at θ to the plane (tan θ = 3/4): find the tension in terms of m and g
parts.ms: M1A1 vertical: R + T sin θ = mg; M1A1 horizontal: T cos θ − F = 0; B1 F = ⅓R; DM1 solve for T in terms of mg; A1 mg/3 (MS p.13)

parts.ask: The rope is removed and the box is projected along the plane with speed u; after moving d its speed is u/2: find d in terms of u and g
parts.ms: B1 F = ⅓mg; B1 F = ma with a new acceleration (or work done Fd); DM1A1 (u/2)² = u² − 2(g/3)d (or work-energy); A1 9u²/8g (MS p.13)

parts.ask: A moves at 40 km/h due east; B at 20 km/h on a bearing α (tan α = 4/3): find the velocity of B in terms of i and j
parts.final_form: (16i + 12j) km h⁻¹ (12i + 16j without working is M1A0)
parts.ms: M1 both components resolved (20 sin α)i + (20 cos α)j; A1 16i + 12j; answers to (a) and (b) in i, j form, penalised once (MS pp.14-15)

parts.ask: At noon A is at 20j km and B at (10i + 5j) km; A is at r = 20j + 40ti: find s, the position of B at time t
parts.ms: M1 correct structure; A1ft on (a) (MS pp.14-15)

parts.ask: Show that AB = [(10 − 24t)i + (12t − 15)j] km
parts.final_form: printed result exactly, with AB at the start or end
parts.ms: M1 s − r with r and s substituted (r − s allowed for M); A1* (MS pp.14-15)

parts.ask: Show that the boats never collide
parts.final_form: two different t values (5/12 and 5/4) so no collision; or no real roots shown
parts.ms: M1 set both components of AB to zero (or r = s); A1 t = 5/12 (0.42 or better) and t = 5/4 (or one used in the other); A1* conclusion; ALT |AB|² = 0 with discriminant shown negative, or minimum distance √80 > 0 (MS pp.14-15)

parts.ask: Find the distance between the boats when the bearing of B from A is 225°
parts.ms: M1 equal components 10 − 24t = 12t − 15; A1 t = 25/36 (0.69); M1 substitute into AB; A1 20√2/3 or 9.4 or better (MS pp.14-15)

parts.ask: A (2m) on a rough plane (tan α = 5/12, μ = 11/36) joined over a smooth pulley at the top to B (3m) hanging at height h above the ground; A moves up the plane after release: show that the friction on A is 22mg/39
Write down an equation of motion for B
parts.ms: M1 correct terms, sign errors condoned; A1 correct (MS pp.16-17)

parts.ask: Show that the acceleration of A immediately after release is g/3
parts.final_form: printed g/3, with sin α = 5/13 seen
parts.ms: M1A1 equation of motion for A: T − 22mg/39 − 2mg sin α = 2ma (or system 3mg − 22mg/39 − 2mg sin α = 5ma); M1 solve for a = kg with trig substituted; A1* (full verification allowed) (MS pp.16-17)

parts.ask: A comes to rest before reaching the pulley: find, in terms of h, the total distance A travels from release until it first comes to rest
parts.ms: B1 v² = 2gh/3 when B lands; M1A1 new equation of motion for A with the string slack: −22mg/39 − 2mg sin α = 2ma, a = −2g/3 (or PE gain 2mgd sin α); M1A1 0 = 2gh/3 − 2(2g/3)d, d = h/2 (or work-energy); A1ft total h + h/2 = 3h/2 (MS pp.16-17)

parts.ask: A (4m, speed 2x) and B (3m, speed x) move towards each other and collide directly; afterwards A has speed y and B speed 5y, both reversed: show y = 5x/11
parts.final_form: printed y = 5x/11 (x in the denominator is A0)
parts.ms: M1 CLM or equate impulses (sign errors, missing m, extra g condoned); A1 4m(2x) − 3mx = 3m(5y) − 4my, all four terms; A1* given answer from working with m seen (MS p.7)

parts.ask: Find, in terms of m and x, the magnitude of the impulse received by A
parts.ms: M1 I = mv − mu with matching mass and velocities (M0 if mass m used, g included or m missing); A1 e.g. 4m(5x/11 + 2x); A1 108mx/11 or 9.8mx or better (MS p.7)

parts.ask: Non-uniform beam AB (6 m, 50 kg) on supports at C and D (AC = 0.9 m, DB = 1.8 m), child of 25 kg at the midpoint E; centre of mass x m from D between C and D; 2R_D = 3R_C: show x = 1.38
parts.ms: M1A1 first equation, e.g. R_C + R_D = 75g (A0 if R_C = R_D assumed; 3R_C + 2R_D = 75g is M0A0); M1A1 moments equation, e.g. M(D): 50gx + 25g(1.2) = 3.3R_C; M1 use 2R_D = 3R_C (R_C = 30g) to an equation in x only; A1* cso; using 2R_C = 3R_D gives 2.37 (max 5/6) (MS pp.8-9)

parts.ask: With the child still at E, a block of mass M kg is placed at B and the beam is on the point of tilting: find M
parts.ms: M1 equation in M only with R_C = 0 (e.g. moments about D, or two equations with R_D eliminated); A1 M(D): 25g(1.2) + 50g(1.38) = 1.8Mg; A1 55 (MS pp.8-9)

parts.ask: Ship A has constant velocity; at 1 pm it is at (25i + 10j) km and at 3 pm at (55i + 34j) km: show its position t hours after 1 pm is rA = (25 + 15t)i + (10 + 12t)j
parts.final_form: printed result (column-vector notation for i, j caps at M1A1M1A0)
parts.ms: M1 v = (r − r0)/2; A1 v = 15i + 12j; M1 rA = (25i + 10j) + t(15i + 12j) with correct structure; A1* given answer (MS p.10)

parts.ask: The speed of A is V m s⁻¹: find V
parts.final_form: V = 5√41/6 ≈ 5.3 m s⁻¹ (5.3 or better; note km/h to m/s)
parts.ms: M1 Pythagoras on their v; A1 √(12² + 15²) × 1000/3600 = 5√41/6, 5.3 or better (MS p.10)

parts.ask: Ship B has velocity (20i − 6j) km/h and is at (35i + 51j) km at 1 pm; at 2:30 pm it passes P: show that A also passes through P
parts.final_form: conclusion that A passes through P (both components give t = 8/3, or rA(8/3) = 65i + 42j)
parts.ms: M1A1 rB at t = 1.5: (35i + 51j) + 1.5(20i − 6j) = 65i + 42j; M1 set rA = rP and solve one component for t; A1 t = 8/3 for one component (t = 2.7 or better allowed for this A1, not for the A1*); A1* t = 8/3 for both components (or substitute) and conclude (MS pp.10-11)

parts.ask: Cyclist P starts from rest at A, accelerates uniformly for 9 s to V m/s, then constant speed; passes B (AB = 120 m) at t = 42: show V = 3.2
parts.ms: M1 area = distance (or suvat) to an equation in V only, e.g. ½(42 + 33)V = 120; A1 correct; A1* given answer (no intermediate line required beyond a correct equation) (MS p.12)

parts.ask: Find the acceleration of P for 0 ≤ t ≤ 9
parts.ms: M1 3.2/9; A1 0.36 or better (MS p.12)

parts.ask: Cyclist Q leaves A at t = 6, accelerates for T s to 3.6 m/s then constant speed, catching P at t = 54: sketch both speed-time graphs for 0 ≤ t ≤ 54 on Figure 2
parts.final_form: Q: starts at t = 6 on the axis, rises to a horizontal line at 3.6 above P's line; P extended to 54; 6, 3.6 and 54 marked
parts.ms: B1 shape for Q (not starting at the origin; horizontal part above P's); DB1 3.6 and 6 marked; B1 P's line extended, both ending at t = 54 marked; continuous vertical lines withhold the first B1 (MS p.12)

parts.ask: Find the value of T
parts.ms: B1 distance of P at t = 54: 158.4 m; M1A1 distance of Q in T only using area or suvat over 6 ≤ t ≤ 54, e.g. ½(48 + 48 − T) × 3.6; DM1 equate and solve; A1 8 (MS p.13)

parts.ask: P (3 kg) and Q (5 kg) on a light inextensible string over a small smooth fixed pulley, released from rest; P moves up with acceleration a and tension T: write down an equation of motion for P
parts.ms: M1 all terms, sign errors condoned; A1 correct; using 3m and 5m consistently caps each part (MS p.14)

parts.ask: Find the value of T
parts.ms: M1A1 equation of motion for Q: 5g − T = 5a (or system 2g = 8a); DM1 solve for T; A1 36.8 or 37 or 15g/4 (MS p.14)

parts.ask: The total force on the pulley due to the string has magnitude F N: find F
parts.ms: M1 F = 2T; A1ft 73.5 or 74, numerical (MS p.14)

parts.ask: Q starts 10 m above the ground; when Q has descended 2 m the string breaks and Q falls: find Q's speed when it hits the ground
parts.ms: B1 a = g/4 used in (d); M1A1ft v² = 2(g/4)(2) (M0 if s = 8); M1 then w² = v² + 2g(8) with a = g; A1 12.9 or 13 (MS p.14)

parts.ask: Particle of mass 5 kg on a rough plane (tan α = 3/4, μ = 1/4) held in equilibrium by a horizontal force H N: find the smallest possible H
parts.final_form: H = 40g/19 = 20.6, 20.7 or 21 (exact multiple of g allowed; 392/19 is A0)
parts.ms: M1A1 perpendicular: R = 5g cos α + H sin α; M1A1 parallel: H cos α + F = 5g sin α (friction up the plane for the minimum); B1 F = ¼R; A1 20.6/20.7/21 or 40g/19; horizontal/vertical resolution also accepted (MS p.15)

parts.ask: H is removed and P slides down from rest, covering 1.5 m in the first T seconds: find T
parts.ms: B1 new reaction S = 5g cos α = 4g; B1 F = ¼S (no marks if R and F from (a) are reused); M1A1 5g sin α − g = 5a, a = 2g/5 = 3.92; M1 1.5 = ½aT²; A1 0.875 or 0.87 (MS pp.15-16)

parts.ask: Ball A is projected vertically up at 8 m/s from the ground and lands first at t = T1: show T1 = 1.63 to 3 s.f.
parts.ms: M1 complete suvat method (e.g. 0 = 8T1 − 4.9T1², or double the time to the top); A1* 1.63 (MS p.17)

parts.ask: A (0.1 kg) rebounds to a height of 2 m: find the magnitude of the impulse from its first impact with the ground
parts.ms: M1 rebound speed from 0 = u² − 2g(2) (energy allowed); A1 u = √(2g × 2) ≈ 6.26; DM1 I = mv − mu; A1 0.1(8 − (−6.3)) with 8 and 6.3 or better; A1 1.4 or 1.43 (MS p.17)

parts.ask: Ball B is projected vertically up at 5 m/s from the ground at t = 1 s; A and B are first at the same height at t = T2 > 1: find T2
parts.final_form: T2 = 1.5 or 1.46 (2 or 3 s.f.; the exact fraction is A0)
parts.ms: M1 equate heights with consistent times (A has been moving for T2, B for T2 − 1; M0 for the same time for both); A1 one height, A1 both: 8T2 − ½gT2² = 5(T2 − 1) − ½g(T2 − 1)²; A1 1.5 or 1.46; ALT from A's height 3.1 m and velocity 1.8 m/s downwards at t = 1 (MS pp.17-18)

parts.ask: Particle of mass 2.5 kg on a smooth horizontal plane acted on by F1 = (6i + 8j), F2 = (−16i + 2j), F3 = (−2i + 8j) N: find the magnitude of its acceleration
parts.ms: M1 sum the forces (−12i + 18j); M1 N2L in vector or scalar form; M1 Pythagoras on a or on R; A1 8.7 or better, exact 12√13/5 (MS p.7)

parts.ask: A fourth force (pi + pj) N is added; the resultant is parallel to (7i + 2j) (Clarification Notice replaced "acts in the direction of"): find p
parts.ms: M1 resultant (−12 + p)i + (18 + p)j with components collected; M1 ratio equation in p only using 7 and 2 (sign error and reciprocal condoned; λ method allowed); A1 (−12 + p)/(18 + p) = 7/2; A1 −30 (MS p.7)

parts.ask: A motorbike passes A at 5 m/s, accelerates uniformly to V m/s at B (time T1), then decelerates uniformly to rest at C (time T2): sketch the speed-time graph from A to C
parts.final_form: graph starting at speed 5 on the vertical axis (not the origin), peak V, ending on the t-axis; T1, T2 (or delineators) and 5, V labelled
parts.ms: B1 shape, starting on the vertical axis above the origin and finishing on the t-axis, no extra continuous lines; B1 time labels; B1 speed labels (MS pp.8-9)

parts.ask: AB = 132 m and BC = 136 m: find, in terms of V, expressions for (i) T1 and (ii) T2
parts.ms: M1 132 = ½(5 + V)T1 (area or suvat; M0 for ½(5 + 5 + V)T1); A1 T1; M1 136 = ½VT2; A1 T2 (MS pp.8-9)

parts.ask: The journey A to C takes 28 s: find V
parts.ms: M1 264/(5 + V) + 272/V = 28 to a quadratic (7V² − 96V − 340 = 0); A1 17, negative root rejected (MS pp.8-9)

parts.ask: Find the deceleration of the motorbike
parts.ms: M1 V/T2 or V²/272 with their V; A1 positive, 1.1 or better (MS pp.8-9)

parts.ask: P (3m kg) and Q (m kg) at rest 1.4 m apart on a rough horizontal surface; an impulse λ N s on P towards Q gives P speed 5 m/s: find λ in terms of m
parts.ms: M1 I = mv − mu with 3m and 5 (M0 if g included or m missing); A1 15m (MS p.10)

parts.ask: P's speed just before hitting Q is 2.5 m/s; μ between P and the surface: find μ
parts.ms: M1A1 suvat for a: 2.5² = 5² + 2a(1.4) (a = −375/56); B1 R = 3mg; M1 F = μR; M1A1 N2L −μ(3mg) = 3ma with consistent direction; A1 0.68 or 0.683 (MS pp.10-11)

parts.ask: Immediately after the collision Q has speed 2.1 m/s: find the speed of P
parts.ms: M1 CLM 3m(2.5) = 3mv + m(2.1), or equate impulses, correct pairings; A1 correct; A1 1.8 (MS pp.10-11)

parts.ask: Uniform rod AB (3 m, weight W N) hangs horizontally from vertical ropes at A and C (AC = 2.1 m); tension at C is 350 N: show W = 490
parts.ms: M1 equation in W only (extra g is an A error), e.g. M(A): 350 × 2.1 = 1.5W; A1 correct; A1* cso (MS pp.12-13)

parts.ask: A particle of weight 210 N is attached d m from A and the tension at C becomes 600 N: find d
parts.ms: M1 equation in d only, e.g. M(A): 600 × 2.1 = 490 × 1.5 + 210d (or eliminate T_A = 100); A1 correct; A1 2.5 (MS pp.12-13)

parts.ask: The particle is removed and a particle of weight X N is attached at B; the rod is on the point of tilting: find X
parts.ms: B1 tension at A is zero (M0 if never used); M1A1 M(C): 490 × 0.6 = 0.9X; A1 980/3 or 330 or better (MS pp.12-13)

parts.ask: A ball modelled as a particle with constant velocity is at (−2i + 5j) m at t = 1 s and (10i − 3j) m at t = 9 s: find its velocity
parts.ms: M1 difference of positions over time (M0 for dividing by 9 instead of 8); A1 [(10i − 3j) − (−2i + 5j)]/8; A1 1.5i − j (MS p.14)

parts.ask: The target is at (13i − 5j) m: use the model to find the distance of the ball from the target at t = 7 s
parts.ms: M1 position at t = 7 from a given position plus k·v (e.g. (−2i + 5j) + 6v); A1 7i − j; M1 Pythagoras between B and T; A1 √52, 2√13 or 7.2 or better (MS p.14)

parts.ask: Particle of mass m held on a rough plane inclined at α (< 45°) by a string at angle α to the plane; with tension 0.75mg it is about to move up the plane: find the friction magnitude in terms of m, g, α
parts.final_form: F = 0.75mg cos α − mg sin α
parts.ms: M1 resolve parallel to the plane (sin/cos confusion and sign errors condoned); A1 at most one error (sin/cos reversed or missing g count as one error); A1 correct (MS pp.15-16)

parts.ask: μ = 1/2: show that tan α = 2/5
parts.ms: M1A1 R = mg cos α − 0.75mg sin α (string pulls away from the plane); B1 F = ½R; M1A1 0.75mg cos α − mg sin α = ½(mg cos α − 0.75mg sin α); A1* cso, sin α and cos α terms collected before the given answer (MS pp.15-16)

parts.ask: The string breaks: determine whether P remains at rest, justifying the answer
parts.final_form: remains at rest, justified by an inequality: ½mg cos α ≈ 0.464mg > mg sin α ≈ 0.371mg (or ½ > tan α = 2/5)
parts.ms: M1 new maximum friction μmg cos α and the weight component mg sin α (M0 if the old R is used); A1 both evaluated and compared or differenced (an inequality or difference must be seen, words alone are not sufficient); A1 conclusion with a valid reason (MS pp.15-16)

parts.ask: A (2m) and B (3m) on a string over a small smooth fixed pulley, both 0.5 m above a horizontal surface; released from rest with B descending: find the tension in terms of m and g
parts.ms: M1A1 first equation of motion (A: T − 2mg = 2ma; B: 3mg − T = 3ma; or system mg = 5ma); M1A1 second; A1 12mg/5; m consistently missing scores M marks only (MS pp.17-18)

parts.ask: Find the speed of B as it strikes the surface
parts.ms: B1 a = g/5 used; M1 v² = 2a(0.5) with their a (M0 if a = 9.8); A1 v² = 1.96; A1 1.4 cao (MS pp.17-18)

parts.ask: B does not rebound and A does not reach the pulley: find the time from release until A first reaches 1.06 m above the surface
parts.ms: M1A1 time for the first 0.5 m with a = g/5 (t = 5/7 ≈ 0.714); M1A1ft A then moves freely under gravity a further 0.06 m: 0.06 = 1.4t − ½gt² (0.56 m also allowed for M; M0 for u = 0 or v = 0); A1 t = 0.0525 (0.233 rejected); A1 total 0.77 or 0.767 (MS pp.17-18)

parts.ask: P (km, speed 5u) catches Q (3m, speed 2u) moving the same way; after the direct collision P has speed 2u (same direction); impulse on Q has magnitude 4.5mu: find Q's speed v in terms of u
parts.ms: M1 impulse on Q (correct masses, speeds and pairings; consistent missing m allowed); A1 4.5mu = 3mv − 3m × 2u; A1 3.5u oe (MS p.8)

parts.ask: Find the value of k
parts.ms: M1 impulse on P, or CLM using v in terms of u; A1 −4.5mu = km × 2u − km × 5u (or km·5u + 3m·2u = km·2u + 3m·3.5u); A1 1.5 oe; (b) may be done first (MS p.8)

parts.ask: A moves with constant velocity; position r = (−5i + 16j) m at t = 2 and (10i + 4j) m at t = 5: find the velocity of A
parts.final_form: (5i − 4j) m s⁻¹, in i, j form
parts.ms: M1 ⅓[(10i + 4j) − (−5i + 16j)] (wrong-order subtraction condoned); A1 5i − 4j; column vectors not accepted in the answers to (a) and (b) (MS p.9)

parts.ask: Find r at time t in the form pi + qj with p and q functions of t
parts.ms: M1 position at a known time plus (t − t₀)v with correct structure; A1 simplified form (MS p.9)

parts.ask: B has position s = −5i + 7j + t(2i − 3j): find, to the nearest degree, the bearing of B from A when t = 5
parts.ms: M1 AB (or BA) at t = 5 (AB = −5i − 12j), using the given r at t = 5; M1 trig for a relevant angle (tan⁻¹(5/12) etc.); A1 203 (MS p.9)

parts.ask: Particle projected vertically up at U m/s from A, 12 m above ground point B; it hits the ground at B after 4 s: find U
parts.ms: M1 suvat to an equation in U only; A1 −12 = 4U − ½g × 16; A1 16.6 or 17 (MS p.10)

parts.ask: Find the speed of the particle as it hits the ground at B
parts.ms: M1 suvat to an equation in the speed/velocity only (allowed even if U came from a wrong method); A1 e.g. −v = 16.6 − 4g or v² = 16.6² + 2g × 12; A1 22.6 or 23 (MS p.10)

parts.ask: Sketch a speed-time graph from leaving A to reaching B (no further calculation needed)
parts.final_form: V shape with vertex on the t-axis, longer second line, values 4, 16.6, 22.6 marked
parts.ms: B1 V shape, equal-magnitude gradients, longer second line, vertex on the t-axis (B0 for a continuous vertical line at t = 4); B1ft 4, 16.6 and 22.6 marked (MS p.10)

parts.ask: A barge is pulled along a canal by two horizontal ropes, 800 N at 25° and 500 N at α° on the other side of the direction of motion: find α
parts.final_form: α = 43 or better, correctly rounded (α = 42.5465...); an answer ending in "..." is A0
parts.ms: M1 resolve perpendicular to the motion, both forces resolved (or sine rule on the vector triangle); M0 for 800cos 25 + 500cos α = 0; A1 800 sin 25° = 500 sin α; A1 43 or better; ending the answer with "..." is A0 (MS p.11)

parts.ask: Barge mass 15 tonnes, constant resistance 750 N: find its acceleration
parts.final_form: 0.023 m s⁻² or better, correctly rounded ("0.02289..." is A0)
parts.ms: M1 F = ma along the motion with both tensions resolved (15 or wrong zeros for the mass condoned; extra g is an A error); A1 at most one error; A1 800cos 25° + 500cos α − 750 = 15000a (or sine/cosine-rule resultant); A1 0.023 or better (use of "..." penalised once per question); a random α in place of (a) caps at A1A0 (MS p.11)

parts.ask: Non-uniform rod AB (length 3a, weight W, centre of mass d from A) rests on a ledge with edge at C (AC = 2a): an upward force P at B puts it on the point of tilting about A; a downward force 1.25P at B puts it on the point of tilting about C: find d in terms of a
parts.final_form: d = 24a/17 (1.4a or better; 6a/4.25 not accepted as final)
parts.ms: M1A1 first case (reaction at C zero, tilting about A): equation in a, d, P, W only, e.g. 3aP = dW; M1A1 second case (reaction at A zero): 1.25Pa = W(2a − d); DM1 solve for d; A1 24a/17; W replaced by Mg allowed, but Wg with P caps at M1A0M1A0DM1A0 (MS p.12)

parts.ask: Package of mass m projected up a rough plane (tan θ = 3/4, μ = 1/4) from A towards B: show that its deceleration is 4g/5
parts.final_form: printed result 4g/5 (0.8g is A0); with −a, allow −a = 4g/5 not a = −4g/5
parts.ms: M1 R = mg cos θ; M1 F = μR; A1 F = ¼mg × ⅘; M1A1 equation of motion F + mg sin θ = ma; A1* 4g/5 from fully correct working including cos θ = 4/5, sin θ = 3/5; just stating F = ⅕mg scores M0M0A0 (MS p.13)

parts.ask: P comes to rest at B with AB = 1.5 m: find the projection speed U
parts.final_form: U = 4.8 or 4.85 (2 or 3 s.f. only; surd forms not accepted)

parts.ask: P (mass 2 kg) is held at rest at B by a force X N acting up the plane: find the smallest possible X
parts.ms: M1 resolve parallel to the slope with friction up the plane, X + F = 2g sin θ (M0 if R appears); A1 X + ¼ × 2g cos θ = 2g sin θ; A1 7.8 or 7.84 (4g/5 allowed) (MS p.14)

parts.ask: Boat A has velocity vA = 2i + 3j + (i − 4j)t km/h: find the magnitude of its acceleration
parts.ms: M1 √(1² + 4²) for the correct vector (or a sign slip); A1 √17 or 4.1 or better (MS p.15)

parts.ask: B has constant acceleration; velocity (4i + j) at t = 2 and (i − 5j) at t = 5: find its acceleration
parts.final_form: (−i − 2j) km h⁻², in i, j form
parts.ms: M1 change of velocity over 3 h (reverse subtraction condoned); A1 −i − 2j (MS p.15)

parts.ask: Find the velocity of B at t = 0
parts.final_form: (6i + 5j) km h⁻¹, in i, j form
parts.ms: M1 back-substitution with their acceleration; A1 6i + 5j, isw a speed; column vectors in (b)/(c) answers penalised once (MS p.15)

parts.ask: At time T1 both boats have the same speed: find the exact value of T1
parts.ms: M1 both velocities in component form: vA = (2 + t)i + (3 − 4t)j, vB = (6 − t)i + (5 − 2t)j; M1 equate squared magnitudes; A1ft T² + T − 4 = 0 or unsimplified; A1 (−1 + √17)/2 cao (MS p.15)

parts.ask: At time T2 both boats move in the same direction: show 3T2² + pT2 + q = 0 and find the integers p and q
parts.ms: M1 ratio of components equal, equation in T2 only (reciprocal on one side allowed); A1ft (5 − 2T)/(6 − T) = (3 − 4T)/(2 + T); A1* 3T2² − 14T2 + 4 = 0 from full working, with the expanded line seen (MS pp.15-16)

sources.qp: drive:25_06_QP_M1.pdf (id 1d6458I71Yn9W8edol4FyKorsvCGvKX8j) = local:src/WME01/2025-06_01_qp.pdf (WME01/01, P81264A, Tuesday 6 May 2025, 32 pp.); same file size as drive "2506 WME01_01 IAL Mechanics M1 June 2025 (pdf).pdf" (ids 1MKcaQ2VUvAZQWuX5nH8jLQ0NZWR49k32, 1bg2MAYWlLVZCadun1pUf9GO_ywZMt_Dv)

parts.ask: Balls P (kM) and Q (3M), k < 3, hang from a light inextensible string over a fixed smooth pulley; released from rest, P accelerates at g/5: write down an equation of motion for P
parts.ms: M1 correct mass, all terms (a for g/5 allowed for M); A1 correct, with g/5 (MS p.17)

parts.ask: Find the value of k
parts.ms: M1 equation of motion for Q (3Mg − T = 3M(g/5)) or for the whole system; A1 correct; A1 2 (MS p.17)

parts.ask: With M = 0.5 kg, find the magnitude of the force exerted on the pulley by the string while Q is moving down
parts.ms: M1 equation for T using k = 2 and M = 0.5 (T − g = g/5 or 1.5g − T = 1.5 × g/5); M1 force on pulley = 2T (independent); A1 23.5 or 24 (12g/5 allowed) (MS p.17)

parts.ask: Q starts 2.5 m above the ground and rebounds at 0.4 m/s after hitting it: find the magnitude of the impulse received by Q
parts.ms: M1A1 speed at impact from v² = 2(g/5)(2.5): v = √g ≈ 3.13; M1A1 impulse = 1.5(0.4 − (−v)) (mass 3M, M or 0.5 condoned for M); A1 5.3 or 5.30 (MS pp.17-18)

parts.ask: P does not hit the pulley: find the total time from release until P first comes to rest
parts.ms: M1 suvat with the correct acceleration for a relevant time: t1 = 5/√g ≈ 1.60 (Q falls 2.5 m with a = g/5) or t2 = 1/√g ≈ 0.32 (P moves freely under gravity after the string slackens); A1 either; M1 total t1 + t2 with correct accelerations; A1 1.9 or 1.92 (MS p.18)

parts.ask: Uniform beam AB (weight 240 N, length 8 m) held horizontal by vertical ropes at C and D (AC = 2 m, DB = x m); tension at D is 90 N: show that x = 2/3
parts.ms: M1 moments (or moments plus vertical) to an equation in x only, e.g. M(C): 240 × 2 = (6 − x) × 90; A1 correct unsimplified; A1* given answer with at least one line of intermediate working and "x =" (MS p.8)

parts.ask: Rope C breaks if its tension exceeds 183 N; a package of weight W N is hung at A and the beam stays in equilibrium: find the greatest possible W
parts.ms: M1 equation in W only with T_C = 183 (M0 if 183 never used, or 90 or 150 used; Wg is an A error), e.g. M(D): 240 × 10/3 + W × 22/3 = 183 × 16/3; A1 at most one error; A1 correct; A1 24 cao; inequalities allowed for the first three marks but equality needed for the last (MS pp.8-9)

sources.qp: drive:25_10_QP_M1.pdf (id 1GEgrltLX26G8FVYDZrqd_s5fey8GuxuW) = local:src/WME01/2025-10_01_qp.pdf (WME01/01, P78844A, Monday 13 October 2025, 28 pp.); same file size as drive "2510 WME01_01 IAL Mechanics M1 October 2025 (pdf).pdf" (ids 1Mw8PejMm0IESvW8fQSEQqmIvABm2sOyV, 1pVUQHgiWCu4K2sQzAKAch9I-TsQXVCSd)

parts.ask: P (7m, speed ku) and Q (3m, speed u) move towards each other and collide; afterwards P has speed w and Q speed 2w with Q reversed; impulse on Q has magnitude 7mu/2: find w in terms of u
parts.final_form: w = u/12 (0.083u or better), a single fraction or decimal
parts.ms: M1 impulse-momentum for Q, dimensionally correct with subtraction (M0 for P, or mass m); A1 7mu/2 = 3m(2w + u); A1 u/12; masses and velocities must be correctly paired throughout (MS p.10)

parts.ask: Find the two possible values of k
parts.final_form: k = 7/12 or k = 5/12 (both, from the two possible directions of P)
parts.ms: M1 impulse-momentum for P or CLM for one valid direction of P after impact, with w substituted; A1ft correct equation; A1 7/12 (0.58 or better); M1 second option with P's velocity of opposite sign; A1 5/12 (0.42 or better) (MS pp.10-11)

sources.qp: drive:25_10_QP_M1.pdf (id 1GEgrltLX26G8FVYDZrqd_s5fey8GuxuW) = local:src/WME01/2025-10_01_qp.pdf (WME01/01, P78844A, Monday 13 October 2025, 28 pp.); same file size as drive "2510 WME01_01 IAL Mechanics M1 October 2025 (pdf).pdf" (ids 1Mw8PejMm0IESvW8fQSEQqmIvABm2sOyV, 1pVUQHgiWCu4K2sQzAKAch9I-TsQXVCSd)
sources.ms: drive:25_10_MS_M1.pdf (id 1KKvXiXNp8XtJzxGH61Sok_1-HdbbHCrV) = local:src/WME01/2025-10_01_ms.pdf (Mark Scheme (Results) October 2025, WME01/01, log P78844A, 22 pp.); same file size as drive "WME01_01_IAL Mechanics M1 October 2025 Mark Scheme (pdf).pdf" (id 15Nc9aWRDeMltyje9vBnuJugcWqh3fpwj)

parts.ask: Particle of mass 2 kg on a smooth horizontal surface acted on by F1 = (−2i + 3j) N and F2 = (4i + 2j) N: find its acceleration
parts.ms: B1 resultant (2i + 5j); M1 F = ma with forces added; A1 i + 2.5j, isw if magnitude found (MS p.12)

parts.ask: Velocity at t = 0 is (3i − 4j) m/s: find the speed when t = 3 s
parts.ms: M1 v = u + at in vector form; A1ft (3i − 4j) + 3(i + 2.5j); DM1 Pythagoras; A1 6.95 or √193/2 (MS p.12)

parts.ask: An extra force F3 = (bi + cj) N makes the resultant λ(i + j) N: show b − c = 3
parts.ms: B1 resultant (2 + b)i + (5 + c)j; M1 equal components, 2 + b = 5 + c, or eliminate λ (M0 for a numerical λ or 2 + b = −(5 + c)); A1* from correct working (MS p.12)

parts.ask: The resultant has magnitude 10√2 N: find the two possible F3
parts.ms: M1A1ft 200 = (2 + b)² + (5 + c)² (or 200 = 2λ²); DM1 equation in one unknown, or use λ = ±10; A1 both forces; one force only scores M1A1M1A0 (MS pp.12-13)

sources.qp: drive:25_10_QP_M1.pdf (id 1GEgrltLX26G8FVYDZrqd_s5fey8GuxuW) = local:src/WME01/2025-10_01_qp.pdf (WME01/01, P78844A, Monday 13 October 2025, 28 pp.); same file size as drive "2510 WME01_01 IAL Mechanics M1 October 2025 (pdf).pdf" (ids 1Mw8PejMm0IESvW8fQSEQqmIvABm2sOyV, 1pVUQHgiWCu4K2sQzAKAch9I-TsQXVCSd)
sources.ms: drive:25_10_MS_M1.pdf (id 1KKvXiXNp8XtJzxGH61Sok_1-HdbbHCrV) = local:src/WME01/2025-10_01_ms.pdf (Mark Scheme (Results) October 2025, WME01/01, log P78844A, 22 pp.); same file size as drive "WME01_01_IAL Mechanics M1 October 2025 Mark Scheme (pdf).pdf" (id 15Nc9aWRDeMltyje9vBnuJugcWqh3fpwj)

parts.ask: P is projected vertically upwards at 5 m/s from A, 10 m above the ground, moving freely under gravity: find its greatest height above A
parts.final_form: 1.3 or 1.28 m (above A; no isw if 10 added)
parts.ms: M1 suvat to an equation in h only (0 = 5² − 2gh); A1 correct; A1 1.3 or 1.28 (MS p.14)

parts.ask: At t = 1 s, Q is projected vertically upwards at 7 m/s from B on the ground directly below A; P and Q collide at t = T: find T
parts.ms: M1 suvat displacement for one particle in T (or t, consistently); M1 the other particle in the same variable (Q has been moving for T − 1); A1 10 + 5T − ½gT² = 7(T − 1) − ½g(T − 1)²; A1 1.9 or 1.86; ALTs start from positions at t = 1 or t = 0 (MS pp.14-15)

parts.ask: Find the speed of P immediately before the collision
parts.ms: M1 v = 5 − gT (or −5 + gT) with their T (M0 for 5 + gT); A1 13 or 13.2 (MS p.15)

sources.qp: drive:25_10_QP_M1.pdf (id 1GEgrltLX26G8FVYDZrqd_s5fey8GuxuW) = local:src/WME01/2025-10_01_qp.pdf (WME01/01, P78844A, Monday 13 October 2025, 28 pp.); same file size as drive "2510 WME01_01 IAL Mechanics M1 October 2025 (pdf).pdf" (ids 1Mw8PejMm0IESvW8fQSEQqmIvABm2sOyV, 1pVUQHgiWCu4K2sQzAKAch9I-TsQXVCSd)
sources.ms: drive:25_10_MS_M1.pdf (id 1KKvXiXNp8XtJzxGH61Sok_1-HdbbHCrV) = local:src/WME01/2025-10_01_ms.pdf (Mark Scheme (Results) October 2025, WME01/01, log P78844A, 22 pp.); same file size as drive "WME01_01_IAL Mechanics M1 October 2025 Mark Scheme (pdf).pdf" (id 15Nc9aWRDeMltyje9vBnuJugcWqh3fpwj)

parts.ask: Box of mass 4 kg on a rough horizontal surface (μ = 2/3) pulled by a force P N at 30° above the horizontal: find P when the box is on the point of sliding
parts.ms: M1A1 resolve horizontally P cos 30° = F; M1A1 resolve vertically P sin 30° + R = 4g; DM1 F = ⅔R to an equation in P only; A1 22 or 21.8 (MS p.16)

parts.ask: P is increased to 25 and the box moves: find its acceleration
parts.ms: M1 vertical resolution with 25 (R = 26.7; M0 if (a)'s R reused); M1A1 equation of motion 25cos 30° − F = 4a (M0 if not using 25); DM1 F = ⅔(4g − 25 sin 30°) to an equation in a only; A1 0.96 or 0.963; adding 25 to their P is treated as a misread (MS pp.16-17)

parts.ask: Find the speed of the box when it has moved 1.5 m
parts.ms: M1 v² = 2 × a × 1.5 with their positive a (not g); A1 cso 1.7 or 1.70 (MS p.17)

sources.qp: drive:25_10_QP_M1.pdf (id 1GEgrltLX26G8FVYDZrqd_s5fey8GuxuW) = local:src/WME01/2025-10_01_qp.pdf (WME01/01, P78844A, Monday 13 October 2025, 28 pp.); same file size as drive "2510 WME01_01 IAL Mechanics M1 October 2025 (pdf).pdf" (ids 1Mw8PejMm0IESvW8fQSEQqmIvABm2sOyV, 1pVUQHgiWCu4K2sQzAKAch9I-TsQXVCSd)
sources.ms: drive:25_10_MS_M1.pdf (id 1KKvXiXNp8XtJzxGH61Sok_1-HdbbHCrV) = local:src/WME01/2025-10_01_ms.pdf (Mark Scheme (Results) October 2025, WME01/01, log P78844A, 22 pp.); same file size as drive "WME01_01_IAL Mechanics M1 October 2025 Mark Scheme (pdf).pdf" (id 15Nc9aWRDeMltyje9vBnuJugcWqh3fpwj)

parts.ask: Car velocity-time graph: 0 to 30 m/s over 0-10 s, constant 30 m/s to t = 30, down to 0 at t = 35: find (i) the acceleration for 0 ≤ t ≤ 10 and (ii) the deceleration for 30 ≤ t ≤ 35
parts.final_form: (i) 3 m s⁻², (ii) 6 m s⁻² (positive; −6 is B0)
parts.ms: B1 acceleration 3; B1 deceleration 6, must be positive (MS p.18)

parts.ask: Sketch an acceleration-time graph for 0 ≤ t ≤ 35
parts.final_form: three horizontal segments: 3 on 0-10, 0 on 10-30, −6 on 30-35, values marked
parts.ms: B1ft any two horizontal lines correct; B1ft all three and no other solid lines, with 10, 30, 35, 3, −6 marked (dotted verticals condoned) (MS p.18)

parts.ask: Find the distance travelled for 0 ≤ t ≤ 35
parts.ms: M1 trapezium area ½(20 + 35) × 30 or equivalent; A1 825 (MS p.18)

parts.ask: A motorcycle starts from rest at O when t = 5 with constant acceleration A m/s² and catches the car at t = 20: find A
parts.ms: M1 motorcycle distance ½A × 15² (condone 20 for 15); M1 equate to the car's distance at t = 20 (½ × 10 × 30 + 10 × 30 = 450); A1 correct equation in A; A1 4 (MS pp.18-19)

sources.qp: drive:25_10_QP_M1.pdf (id 1GEgrltLX26G8FVYDZrqd_s5fey8GuxuW) = local:src/WME01/2025-10_01_qp.pdf (WME01/01, P78844A, Monday 13 October 2025, 28 pp.); same file size as drive "2510 WME01_01 IAL Mechanics M1 October 2025 (pdf).pdf" (ids 1Mw8PejMm0IESvW8fQSEQqmIvABm2sOyV, 1pVUQHgiWCu4K2sQzAKAch9I-TsQXVCSd)
sources.ms: drive:25_10_MS_M1.pdf (id 1KKvXiXNp8XtJzxGH61Sok_1-HdbbHCrV) = local:src/WME01/2025-10_01_ms.pdf (Mark Scheme (Results) October 2025, WME01/01, log P78844A, 22 pp.); same file size as drive "WME01_01_IAL Mechanics M1 October 2025 Mark Scheme (pdf).pdf" (id 15Nc9aWRDeMltyje9vBnuJugcWqh3fpwj)

parts.ask: Block P (2m) on a rough plane with tan α = 5/12, joined by a string over a smooth pulley at the top to Q (5m) hanging; released from rest, P moves up the plane with tension T and acceleration a: write down an equation of motion for Q
parts.ms: M1 correct terms, sign errors condoned; A1 correct equation; m missing consistently caps the question (MS p.20)

parts.ask: μ = 1/8: find T in terms of m and g
parts.ms: M1A1 R = 2mg cos α (R = mg cos α is M0); M1 F = ⅛R; M1A1 equation of motion for P: T − F − 2mg sin α = 2ma (combined 5mg − F − 2mg sin α = 7ma condoned); DM1 solve for T using the two equations that earned marks; A1 15mg/7 (MS p.20)

parts.ask: State how the solution to (b) uses the fact that the string is inextensible
parts.final_form: one statement: the blocks have the same acceleration
parts.ms: B1 acceleration of both blocks/particles is the same; "it/the string has the same acceleration" not accepted; B0 with extra wrong statements (same tension, string will not break) (MS p.21)

parts.ask: The force exerted on the pulley by the string has magnitude kmg: find k to 3 significant figures
parts.final_form: k = 3.57 (3 s.f. only; exact form or "3.57mg" is A0)
parts.ms: M1A1 resultant of the two tensions, e.g. 2T cos((90° − α)/2), or cosine rule with angle 90° + α, or components (T cos α)² + (T + T sin α)²; DM1 substitute T and trig and solve, as a multiple of mg; A1 3.57 (MS pp.21-22)

sources.qp: drive:25_10_QP_M1.pdf (id 1GEgrltLX26G8FVYDZrqd_s5fey8GuxuW) = local:src/WME01/2025-10_01_qp.pdf (WME01/01, P78844A, Monday 13 October 2025, 28 pp.); same file size as drive "2510 WME01_01 IAL Mechanics M1 October 2025 (pdf).pdf" (ids 1Mw8PejMm0IESvW8fQSEQqmIvABm2sOyV, 1pVUQHgiWCu4K2sQzAKAch9I-TsQXVCSd)
sources.ms: drive:25_10_MS_M1.pdf (id 1KKvXiXNp8XtJzxGH61Sok_1-HdbbHCrV) = local:src/WME01/2025-10_01_ms.pdf (Mark Scheme (Results) October 2025, WME01/01, log P78844A, 22 pp.); same file size as drive "WME01_01_IAL Mechanics M1 October 2025 Mark Scheme (pdf).pdf" (id 15Nc9aWRDeMltyje9vBnuJugcWqh3fpwj)

parts.ask: P (2m, 4u due east) and Q (3m, u due west) collide directly; the impulse has magnitude 33mu/5: find the speed and direction of P after the collision
parts.final_form: 0.7u due East (speed and direction both stated)
parts.ms: M1 impulse-momentum for P (difference of momenta, M0 if g included) or CLM with masses and velocities correctly paired; A1 correct equation, e.g. −33mu/5 = 2m(v − 4u); A1 0.7u due East: direction must be stated in words (E, unchanged, towards Q); "to the right" or "positive direction" is A0 (MS p.8)

parts.ask: Find the speed and direction of Q after the collision
parts.ms: M1 impulse-momentum for Q (33mu/5 = 3m(v + u)) or CLM; A1 correct equation; A1 1.2u due East, direction in words (E, reverses, opposite direction); "changed direction" alone is A0; (a) and (b) may be marked together (MS pp.8-9)

sources.qp: drive:25_10_QP_M1A.pdf (id 1jvhIbkQv2Y47Jjnk-GXk5VeQcbJo7YTj) = local:src/WME01/2025-10_01A_qp.pdf (regional paper WME01/01A, P87438A, Monday 13 October 2025 afternoon; questions on PDF pp.2-8, followed by the separate answer book P87472A on pp.9-32)
sources.ms: drive:25_10_MS_M1A.pdf (id 1W3HKT56GHJ-DJTZx4GT3gZf9IF8iqX-h) = local:src/WME01/2025-10_01A_ms.pdf (Mark Scheme (Results) October 2025, WME01/01A, WME01_01A_2510_MS, 23 pp.)

parts.ask: Uniform plank AB (6 m, 4 kg) on supports at C and D (AC = 2 m, DB = 1 m) with bricks of 2 kg at A and 3 kg at B: find the reactions at C and at D
parts.ms: Marked together: M1 moments (or vertical) equation in R_C, dimensionally correct with correct number of terms; A1 e.g. M(D): 3R_C + 1·3g = 2·4g + 5·2g; A1 R_C = 49; M1A1A1 likewise R_D = 39/39.2; consistent missing g or m on every mass is an A error (MS pp.10-11)

parts.ask: The 3 kg brick is replaced by one of x kg at B; the reactions at C and D are now equal: find x
parts.ms: M1 moments equation in x and the new reaction(s) (M0 if a reaction from (a) is reused); A1 correct; dM1 complete method using R_C = R_D with a second equation (vertical: R_C + R_D = 4g + 2g + xg); A1 3.6 oe; SC consistent missing g max 4 (MS pp.10-11)

sources.qp: drive:25_10_QP_M1A.pdf (id 1jvhIbkQv2Y47Jjnk-GXk5VeQcbJo7YTj) = local:src/WME01/2025-10_01A_qp.pdf (regional paper WME01/01A, P87438A, Monday 13 October 2025 afternoon; questions on PDF pp.2-8, followed by the separate answer book P87472A on pp.9-32)
sources.ms: drive:25_10_MS_M1A.pdf (id 1W3HKT56GHJ-DJTZx4GT3gZf9IF8iqX-h) = local:src/WME01/2025-10_01A_ms.pdf (Mark Scheme (Results) October 2025, WME01/01A, WME01_01A_2510_MS, 23 pp.)

parts.ask: F1 = (2i − 3j) N and F2 = (pi + qj) N; their resultant is parallel to (i + 2j): show 2p − q + 7 = 0
parts.ms: M1 resultant (p + 2)i + (q − 3)j; M1 parallel condition to an equation in p and q only (reciprocal ratio condoned; multiplier method M0 if λ = 1); A1 correct equation; dM1 complete method; A1* given answer from exact working with at least one intermediate line, must "= 0"; unconventional vector notation is A0 (MS pp.12-13)

parts.ask: Given q = 11 and the 2 kg particle A is acted on only by F1 and F2, find the magnitude of its acceleration
parts.ms: B1 p = 2; M1 resultant (4i + 8j) (M0 if weight included); M1 N2L F = ma with R or |R| (a = 2i + 4j); M1 Pythagoras on a or R (two non-zero components; M0 for |F1| or |F2| alone); A1 √20, 2√5 or 4.5 or better (MS pp.12-13)

sources.qp: drive:25_10_QP_M1A.pdf (id 1jvhIbkQv2Y47Jjnk-GXk5VeQcbJo7YTj) = local:src/WME01/2025-10_01A_qp.pdf (regional paper WME01/01A, P87438A, Monday 13 October 2025 afternoon; questions on PDF pp.2-8, followed by the separate answer book P87472A on pp.9-32)
sources.ms: drive:25_10_MS_M1A.pdf (id 1W3HKT56GHJ-DJTZx4GT3gZf9IF8iqX-h) = local:src/WME01/2025-10_01A_ms.pdf (Mark Scheme (Results) October 2025, WME01/01A, WME01_01A_2510_MS, 23 pp.)

parts.ask: Block A (9 kg) falls from rest from height h and has speed 7 m/s just before striking block B on the ground: find h
parts.ms: M1 suvat to an equation in h (7² = 0² + 2gh); A1 2.5 (MS p.14)

parts.ask: A and B (1.5 kg) move down together and sink 12 cm into the ground; resistance has constant magnitude R N: find R
parts.ms: M1A1 CLM with common velocity: 9 × 7 = 10.5v (v = 6); M1A1 suvat 0 = 6² + 2a(0.12) (a = −150; 12 or 1.2 condoned for M; M0 if u = 7); M1A1 N2L for the combined mass: 10.5g − R = 10.5(−150) (M0 if a = g); A1 1680 or 1700; energy (WME02) method also credited (MS pp.14-15)

sources.qp: drive:25_10_QP_M1A.pdf (id 1jvhIbkQv2Y47Jjnk-GXk5VeQcbJo7YTj) = local:src/WME01/2025-10_01A_qp.pdf (regional paper WME01/01A, P87438A, Monday 13 October 2025 afternoon; questions on PDF pp.2-8, followed by the separate answer book P87472A on pp.9-32)
sources.ms: drive:25_10_MS_M1A.pdf (id 1W3HKT56GHJ-DJTZx4GT3gZf9IF8iqX-h) = local:src/WME01/2025-10_01A_ms.pdf (Mark Scheme (Results) October 2025, WME01/01A, WME01_01A_2510_MS, 23 pp.)

parts.ask: P (0.1 kg) on a rough horizontal table joined over a smooth pulley at the table edge to Q (0.5 kg) on a smooth plane with tan θ = 4/3; Q moves 0.75 m down the plane in the first 0.5 s from rest: find the tension
parts.ms: M1A1 suvat 0.75 = ½a(0.5)² (a = 6); M1 N2L for Q along the plane (M0 if a = g; sin/cos and sign errors condoned); A1ft 0.5g sin θ − T = 0.5a; A1 0.92; if both surfaces taken as rough, max B1M0A0M1A0 overall (MS pp.16-17)

parts.ask: Find the coefficient of friction between P and the table
parts.ms: B1 R = 0.1g; M1A1 N2L for P (T − F = 0.1 × 6) or for the system (0.5g sin θ − F = 0.6 × 6); M1 F = μR used with their R (not just quoted); A1 0.327 or 0.33 (MS pp.16-17)

sources.qp: drive:25_10_QP_M1A.pdf (id 1jvhIbkQv2Y47Jjnk-GXk5VeQcbJo7YTj) = local:src/WME01/2025-10_01A_qp.pdf (regional paper WME01/01A, P87438A, Monday 13 October 2025 afternoon; questions on PDF pp.2-8, followed by the separate answer book P87472A on pp.9-32)
sources.ms: drive:25_10_MS_M1A.pdf (id 1W3HKT56GHJ-DJTZx4GT3gZf9IF8iqX-h) = local:src/WME01/2025-10_01A_ms.pdf (Mark Scheme (Results) October 2025, WME01/01A, WME01_01A_2510_MS, 23 pp.)

parts.ask: Washing line ABCD: 3 kg particle at B, M kg at C, AB at α (tan α = 3/4) and CD at β (tan β = 12/5) to the horizontal, BC horizontal, in equilibrium: find the tension in AB
parts.ms: B1 sin α = 3/5 or cos α = 4/5 (or α = 37° or better); M1 vertical equilibrium at B; A1 T_AB sin α = 3g; A1 49 (MS pp.18-19)

parts.ask: Find the tension in BC
parts.ms: M1 horizontal equilibrium at B (M0 if the same tension is assumed in different sections); A1 T_AB cos α = T_BC; A1 39 or 39.2 (MS pp.18-19)

parts.ask: Find the value of M
parts.ms: M1 equilibrium at C or for the whole system giving an equation in T_CD; A1 one correct, A1 two correct (e.g. T_CD cos β = T_BC, T_CD sin β = Mg); dM1 equation in M only, e.g. tan β = Mg/T_BC (dM0 if T_CD = T_AB used); A1 9.6 (MS pp.18-19)
